The study aimed to evaluate the safety profile of vaccines administered in 2024, with a focus on RSV-related adverse events.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study is a national surveillance report conducted in Australia during 2024, encompassing all vaccines administered in the country. It includes data from the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) on adverse events reported across the population.
analysis_en.methods: AEFI data were collected through spontaneous reporting to the TGA and analysed continuously and annually to identify new safety concerns or changes in known safety issues. The analyses focused on the frequency and types of adverse events associated with vaccines, including RSV vaccines.
analysis_en.main_results: In 2024, there were 6,232 AEFI reports for vaccines administered, with RZV (Shingrix) associated with the highest number of reported AEFIs. The most frequently reported adverse events were medication errors, hypersensitivity, gastrointestinal nonspecific symptoms, pyrexia, and injection site reactions.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the slight increase in AEFI reporting rates in 2024 was likely due to the introduction of the new recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV) and the expansion of the eligible population for zoster vaccination. This finding highlights the importance of monitoring new vaccines for safety signals.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the ongoing surveillance of vaccine safety, particularly for RSV vaccines, and support the need for continued monitoring of adverse events to ensure public health safety and improve vaccine programs.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on spontaneous reporting, which may introduce bias and underreporting. The evidence is moderate as it relies on observational data rather than controlled experiments, and the interpretation is grounded in the observed trends.

title_zh: 监测 2024 年澳大利亚免疫接种后不良事件。
source_body_en: This report summarises Australia's spontaneous surveillance data for adverse events following immunisation (AEFI) for all vaccines administered in 2024, reported to the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA). An adverse event(s) following immunisation is defined as any untoward medical occurrence which follows immunisation but does not necessarily have a causal relationship with use of the vaccine. Analyses of AEFI data are done continuously and also annually to detect new potential safety issues or changes to known safety issues. Overall, there were 6,232 AEFI reports for vaccines administered in 2024. This represents an annual AEFI reporting rate of 22.9 per 100,000 population and 25.7 per 100,000 vaccine doses, compared with 20.8 per 100,000 population and 24.1 per 100,000 doses in 2023. The slight increase in the AEFI reporting rates observed in 2024 was likely driven by the introduction of a new recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, Shingrix) which replaced the live attenuated zoster vaccine (ZLV, Zostavax) on the National Immunisation Program (NIP) from November 2023, along with the expansion of the eligible population for zoster vaccination. In 2024, RZV (Shingrix) was associated with the highest number of reported AEFIs. The most frequently reported adverse events following immunisation were medication errors; hypersensitivity; gastrointestinal nonspecific symptoms; pyrexia; and injection site reaction. Among vaccines newly introduced in 2024, the most commonly reported adverse events were medication errors and nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms for COVID-19 vaccines (Comirnaty XBB.1.5 and Spikevax XBB.1.5); hypersensitivity and pyrexia for the DTPa-HepB-IPV-Hib vaccine (Vaxelis); medication errors and exposure during pregnancy for the adjuvanted recombinant respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) pre-fusion F protein vaccine (Arexvy); and hypersensitivity and nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms for RZV (Shingrix). Fewer deaths were reported following vaccination in 2024 (28 reports) than in 2023 (34 reports). None of the 28 reported deaths in 2024 indicated an emerging safety signal.

title: Immunogenicity of the Foldon trimerization domain and efforts to shield it.
abstract: Protein subunit and mRNA vaccines encoding viral glycoprotein antigens fused to the bacteriophage T4 fibritintrimerization domain are increasingly being tested in human clinical trials. AREXVY and ABRYSVO®, subunit vaccines composed of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prefusion F glycoprotein(s) fused to Foldon, are now FDA-approved and regularly administered. However, administration of vaccine antigens containing the Foldon domain has the potential to elicit off-target antibody responses. Here, we demonstrate that protein subunit vaccine antigens RSV F Foldon and influenza hemagglutinin (HA) Foldon elicit antibodies against the Foldon domain. To dampen Foldon-induced antibody responses, we engineered influenza computationally optimized broadly reactive antigen (COBRA) HA proteins with N-glycosylation motif mutations at three different sites in Foldon. Mass spectrometry analyses confirmed partial occupancy of N-glycosylation modifications at two of the three intended sites. Two of the three COBRA HA Foldon mutant antigens demonstrated reduced binding by anti-Foldon monoclonal and polyclonal antibodies compared to the wild-type COBRA HA Foldon. However, mice immunized with the COBRA HA Foldon mutant antigens did not have a significant reduction in the elicitation of anti-Foldon antibodies. Further analysis suggested that some of the observed differences in antibody binding to mutant Foldon antigens can be attributed to differences in protein sequence alone. Altogether, these data suggest that while the N-glycosylation modifications may partially shield the Foldon from reactive antibodies, this shielding does not significantly reduce its immunogenicity in a naïve setting. Importantly, these data highlight that the Foldon trimerization domain is immunogenic, which should be considered during clinical trials of vaccines that contain Foldon.

However, administration of vaccine antigens containing the Foldon domain has the potential to elicit off-target antibody responses. Here, we demonstrate that protein subunit vaccine antigens RSV F Foldon and influenza hemagglutinin (HA) Foldon elicit antibodies against the Foldon domain. To dampen Foldon-induced antibody responses, we engineered influenza computationally optimized broadly reactive antigen (COBRA) HA proteins with N-glycosylation motif mutations at three different sites in Foldon. Mass spectrometry analyses confirmed partial occupancy of N-glycosylation modifications at two of the three intended sites. Two of the three COBRA HA Foldon mutant antigens demonstrated reduced binding by anti-Foldon monoclonal and polyclonal antibodies compared to the wild-type COBRA HA Foldon. However, mice immunized with the COBRA HA Foldon mutant antigens did not have a significant reduction in the elicitation of anti-Foldon antibodies. Further analysis suggested that some of the observed differences in antibody binding to mutant Foldon antigens can be attributed to differences in protein sequence alone. Altogether, these data suggest that while the N-glycosylation modifications may partially shield the Foldon from reactive antibodies, this shielding does not significantly reduce its immunogenicity in a naïve setting. Importantly, these data highlight that the Foldon trimerization domain is immunogenic, which should be considered during clinical trials of vaccines that contain Foldon.

The researchers engineered influenza HA proteins with N-glycosylation motif mutations in Foldon and evaluated their immunogenicity in mice. Mass spectrometry confirmed partial occupancy of N-glycosylation modifications at two of three intended sites, and antibody binding was assessed. Two of the three mutant antigens showed reduced binding by anti-Foldon antibodies, but mice immunized with these mutants did not have a significant reduction in anti-Foldon antibody elicitation. abstract_zh: 编码与噬菌体 T4 fibritin 三聚化结构域融合的病毒糖蛋白抗原的蛋白质亚基和 mRNA 疫苗 越来越多地在人体临床试验中进行测试。AREXVY 和 ABRYSVO® 亚基 疫苗 由与 Foldon 融合的 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 预融合 F 糖蛋白组成,现已获得 FDA 批准并定期给药。然而,施用含有 Foldon 结构域的 疫苗 抗原有可能引发脱靶抗体反应。在这里,我们证明蛋白质亚基 疫苗 抗原 RSV F Foldon 和流感血凝素 (HA) Foldon 会引发针对 Foldon 结构域的抗体。为了抑制 Foldon 诱导的抗体反应,我们在 Foldon 的三个不同位点设计了具有 N-糖基化基序 突变 的流感计算优化的广泛反应性抗原 (COBRA) HA 蛋白。质谱分析证实 N-糖基化修饰在三个预定位点中的两个位点被部分占据。与野生型 COBRA HA Foldon 相比,三种 COBRA HA Foldon 突变抗原中的两种表现出抗 Foldon 单克隆和多克隆抗体的结合减少。然而,用COBRA HA Foldon突变抗原免疫的小鼠抗Foldon抗体的引发并没有显着减少。进一步的分析表明,观察到的抗体与突变型 Foldon 抗原结合的一些差异可归因于蛋白质序列的差异。总而言之,这些数据表明,虽然 N-糖基化修饰可能部分保护 Foldon 免受反应性抗体的影响,但这种屏蔽并不会显着降低其在初始环境中的免疫原性。重要的是,这些数据强调了 Foldon 三聚化结构域具有免疫原性,在含有 Foldon 的 疫苗 临床试验中应考虑这一点。

title: Genomic diversity of respiratory pathogens in clinical versus community surveillance: a comparative analysis of SARS-CoV-2, RSV, and influenza viruses in Washington State
abstract: BackgroundGenomic surveillance of respiratory viruses typically relies on sequences from individuals seeking health care, and whether these sequences represent the viruses circulating in the community is not well-characterized. We aimed to compare the diversity, proportion, and dynamics of influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 between clinical and community samples. MethodsIn this retrospective comparative genomic analysis, we used whole-genome sequences from community-based surveillance studies in the Seattle area, and clinical sequences from the Washington State Department of Health. We compared clade proportions and dynamics, sequence-cluster diversity, non-synonymous mutations, and Ct values between clinical and community samples. FindingsWe analyzed 538 RSV sequences collected between 2019 and 2021 (278 community, 260 clinical), 1506 influenza sequences (260 community, 1246 clinical) between 2019 and 2020, and 8660 SARS-CoV-2 sequences (5923 community, 2737 clinical) from 2020 to 2022. Clade proportions did not differ between clinical and community samples for RSV or influenza, but differed for SARS-CoV-2: clades 21J (Delta) and 21K (Omicron BA.1) were more frequent in community samples and clade 22B (Omicron BA.5) in clinical samples. SARS-CoV-2 clinical sequence clusters were more diverse than community clusters, whereas RSV and influenza showed no significant difference. Several spike mutations associated with monoclonal antibody resistance were more prevalent in community samples for SARS-CoV-2. Ct values were lower in clinical samples for multiple SARS-CoV-2, RSV, and influenza clades. InterpretationSeasonal respiratory viruses had similar dynamics and diversity in clinical and community samples, whereas pandemic SARS-CoV-2 differed between settings. Genomic surveillance programs should combine clinical and community sampling, particularly during pandemics in order to better capture viral diversity. FundingThis analysis was funded by the Washington State Department of Health Northwest Pathogen Genomics Center of Excellence (WA DOH contract number HED29377-1, federal grant number NU50CK000630 to University of Washington). The underlying studies were funded by Gates Ventures. RESEARCH IN CONTEXTO_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyC_ST_ABSGenomic surveillance of respiratory viruses expanded substantially during the COVID-19 pandemic and has since been extended to respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and influenza, but most sequences come from people who sought medical care. We searched PubMed for studies published in English up to September 2026 using combinations of terms "genomic surveillance", "community surveillance", "respiratory syncytial virus", "influenza", "SARS-CoV-2", "whole genome sequencing", and included studies that sequenced respiratory viruses from defined clinical or community populations. Previous work has sampled hospitalized patients, sequenced random positive specimens, or sequenced wastewater, and has shown that such data can track variant emergence, clade replacement, and nosocomial transmission. However, few studies compared clinical and community sampling for the same virus in the same population and period, so it remains unclear whether clinically derived sequences represent the viruses circulating in the community. Added value of this studyTo our knowledge, this is the first study to compare viral diversity between clinical and community sampling for three respiratory viruses in the same region and overlapping time periods. Using more than 10,000 whole genomes from community-based surveillance studies and state clinical surveillance in Washington State, we found that clade proportions and dynamics were similar between sources for RSV and influenza, but differed for SARS-CoV-2. At finer genetic resolution, clinical SARS-CoV-2 sequences formed more diverse clusters than community sequences, and several spike mutations associated with monoclonal antibody resistance were more prevalent in community samples. Implications of all the available evidenceFor seasonal respiratory viruses, sampling people who seek care appears to capture much of the diversity circulating in the community, which may allow surveillance programs with limited resources to rely on clinical specimens. In contrast with seasonal circulation in a population with some pre-existing immunity, during pandemic-level transmission, when very large numbers of people in a largely susceptible population are infected over a short period, clinical and community samples are not interchangeable, and programs that sequence only clinical specimens risk missing variants circulating in the community, including mutations relevant to antiviral and monoclonal antibody resistance. These differences may partly reflect the much larger number of SARS-CoV-2 genomes available, as well as heterogeneous mixing and co-circulation of multiple variants during the pandemic. Surveillance programs should therefore combine clinical and community sampling, and future studies should test whether these patterns hold in other regions, seasons, and pathogens.

The underlying studies were funded by Gates Ventures. RESEARCH IN CONTEXTO_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyC_ST_ABSGenomic surveillance of respiratory viruses expanded substantially during the COVID-19 pandemic and has since been extended to respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and influenza, but most sequences come from people who sought medical care. We searched PubMed for studies published in English up to September 2026 using combinations of terms "genomic surveillance", "community surveillance", "respiratory syncytial virus", "influenza", "SARS-CoV-2", "whole genome sequencing", and included studies that sequenced respiratory viruses from defined clinical or community populations. However, few studies compared clinical and community sampling for the same virus in the same population and period, so it remains unclear whether clinically derived sequences represent the viruses circulating in the community. Using more than 10,000 whole genomes from community-based surveillance studies and state clinical surveillance in Washington State, we found that clade proportions and dynamics were similar between sources for RSV and influenza, but differed for SARS-CoV-2. In contrast with seasonal circulation in a population with some pre-existing immunity, during pandemic-level transmission, when very large numbers of people in a largely susceptible population are infected over a short period, clinical and community samples are not interchangeable, and programs that sequence only clinical specimens risk missing variants circulating in the community, including mutations relevant to antiviral and monoclonal antibody resistance. These differences may partly reflect the much larger number of SARS-CoV-2 genomes available, as well as heterogeneous mixing and co-circulation of multiple variants during the pandemic. Surveillance programs should therefore combine clinical and community sampling, and future studies should test whether these patterns hold in other regions, seasons, and pathogens.

analysis.summary_en: This study compares the genomic diversity of respiratory viruses between clinical and community samples in Washington State, focusing on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza, and SARS-CoV-2. The research question addresses the gap in understanding whether clinical sequences accurately represent community viral circulation. The study design involves a retrospective comparative genomic analysis using sequences from both clinical and community sources. Whole-genome sequencing was employed to assess clade proportions, sequence-cluster diversity, non-synonymous mutations, and Ct values. The main results show that RSV and influenza had similar clade proportions and diversity in both settings, while SARS-CoV-2 showed differences, with community samples having more frequent clades 21J and 21K, and clinical samples showing more diversity in sequence clusters. The authors interpret these findings as indicating that seasonal respiratory viruses have comparable dynamics in clinical and community settings, but pandemic SARS-CoV-2 differs significantly. The study suggests that genomic surveillance programs should integrate both clinical and community sampling, especially during pandemics, to capture full viral diversity. The evidence strength is moderate, as the study is based on abstract-only data and does not report specific limitations.

We aimed to compare the diversity, proportion, and dynamics of influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 between clinical and community samples. MethodsIn this retrospective comparative genomic analysis, we used whole-genome sequences from community-based surveillance studies in the Seattle area, and clinical sequences from the Washington State Department of Health. We compared clade proportions and dynamics, sequence-cluster diversity, non-synonymous mutations, and Ct values between clinical and community samples. FindingsWe analyzed 538 RSV sequences collected between 2019 and 2021 (278 community, 260 clinical), 1506 influenza sequences (260 community, 1246 clinical) between 2019 and 2020, and 8660 SARS-CoV-2 sequences (5923 community, 2737 clinical) from 2020 to 2022. Clade proportions did not differ between clinical and community samples for RSV or influenza, but differed for SARS-CoV-2: clades 21J (Delta) and 21K (Omicron BA.1) were more frequent in community samples and clade 22B (Omicron BA.5) in clinical samples. SARS-CoV-2 clinical sequence clusters were more diverse than community clusters, whereas RSV and influenza showed no significant difference. Several spike mutations associated with monoclonal antibody resistance were more prevalent in community samples for SARS-CoV-2. Ct values were lower in clinical samples for multiple SARS-CoV-2, RSV, and influenza clades. InterpretationSeasonal respiratory viruses had similar dynamics and diversity in clinical and community samples, whereas pandemic SARS-CoV-2 differed between settings. Genomic surveillance programs should combine clinical and community sampling, particularly during pandemics in order to better capture viral diversity. FundingThis analysis was funded by the Washington State Department of Health Northwest Pathogen Genomics Center of Excellence (WA DOH contract number HED29377-1, federal grant number NU50CK000630 to University of Washington). The underlying studies were funded by Gates Ventures. RESEARCH IN CONTEXTO_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyC_ST_ABSGenomic surveillance of respiratory viruses expanded substantially during the COVID-19 pandemic and has since been extended to respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and influenza, but most sequences come from people who sought medical care. We searched PubMed for studies published in English up to September 2026 using combinations of terms "genomic surveillance", "community surveillance", "respiratory syncytial virus", "influenza", "SARS-CoV-2", "whole genome sequencing", and included studies that sequenced respiratory viruses from defined clinical or community populations. Previous work has sampled hospitalized patients, sequenced random positive specimens, or sequenced wastewater, and has shown that such data can track variant emergence, clade replacement, and nosocomial transmission. However, few studies compared clinical and community sampling for the same virus in the same population and period, so it remains unclear whether clinically derived sequences represent the viruses circulating in the community. Added value of this studyTo our knowledge, this is the first study to compare viral diversity between clinical and community sampling for three respiratory viruses in the same region and overlapping time periods. Using more than 10,000 whole genomes from community-based surveillance studies and state clinical surveillance in Washington State, we found that clade proportions and dynamics were similar between sources for RSV and influenza, but differed for SARS-CoV-2. At finer genetic resolution, clinical SARS-CoV-2 sequences formed more diverse clusters than community sequences, and several spike mutations associated with monoclonal antibody resistance were more prevalent in community samples. Implications of all the available evidenceFor seasonal respiratory viruses, sampling people who seek care appears to capture much of the diversity circulating in the community, which may allow surveillance programs with limited resources to rely on clinical specimens. In contrast with seasonal circulation in a population with some pre-existing immunity, during pandemic-level transmission, when very large numbers of people in a largely susceptible population are infected over a short period, clinical and community samples are not interchangeable, and programs that sequence only clinical specimens risk missing variants circulating in the community, including mutations relevant to antiviral and monoclonal antibody resistance. These differences may partly reflect the much larger number of SARS-CoV-2 genomes available, as well as heterogeneous mixing and co-circulation of multiple variants during the pandemic. Surveillance programs should therefore combine clinical and community sampling, and future studies should test whether these patterns hold in other regions, seasons, and pathogens.
abstract_zh: 背景呼吸道病毒的基因组监测通常依赖于寻求医疗保健的个体的序列,并且这些序列是否代表社区中传播的病毒尚不清楚。我们的目的是比较临床和社区样本之间流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和 SARS-CoV-2 的多样性、比例和动态。方法在这项回顾性比较基因组分析中,我们使用了来自西雅图地区基于社区的 基因组 研究的全 基因组 序列,以及来自华盛顿州卫生部的临床序列。我们比较了临床和社区样本之间的进化枝比例和动态、序列簇多样性、非同义 突变 以及 Ct 值。研究结果我们分析了 2019 年至 2021 年收集的 538 个 RSV 序列(278 个社区,260 个临床),2019 年至 2020 年收集的 1506 个流感序列(260 个社区,1246 个临床),以及 2020 年至 2022 年收集的 8660 个 SARS-CoV-2 序列(5923 个社区,2737 个临床)。进化枝比例没有差异RSV 或流感的临床样本和社区样本之间存在差异,但 SARS-CoV-2 存在差异:社区样本中的进化枝 21J (Delta) 和 21K (Omicron BA.1) 更为常见,而临床样本中的进化枝 22B (Omicron BA.5) 则更为常见。SARS-CoV-2 临床序列簇比社区簇更加多样化,而 RSV 和流感则没有显着差异。与单克隆抗体耐药性相关的几个尖峰 突变 在 SARS-CoV-2 社区样本中更为普遍。多个 SARS-CoV-2、RSV 和流感分支的临床样本中的 Ct 值较低。解释季节性呼吸道病毒在临床和社区样本中具有相似的动态和多样性,而大流行的 SARS-CoV-2 在不同环境中则不同。基因组监测 计划应结合临床和社区采样,特别是在大流行期间,以便更好地捕获病毒多样性。资助本分析由华盛顿州卫生部西北病原体基因组学卓越中心资助(华盛顿州卫生部合同号 HED29377-1,华盛顿大学联邦拨款号 NU50CK000630)。基础研究由盖茨风险投资公司资助。CONTEXTO_ST_ABS 研究之前的证据 C_ST_ABS 呼吸道病毒的基因组 监测 在 COVID-19 大流行期间大幅扩展,此后已扩展到 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和流感,但大多数序列来自寻求医疗护理的人。我们使用术语“基因组监测”、“社区 监测”、“呼吸道合胞病毒”、“流感”、“SARS-CoV-2”、“整个 基因组 测序”的组合检索了 PubMed 中截至 2026 年 9 月以英文发表的研究,并纳入了对来自特定临床或社区人群的呼吸道病毒进行测序的研究。之前的工作对住院患者进行了采样,对随机阳性样本进行了测序,或对废水进行了测序,并表明这些数据可以跟踪变异的出现、进化枝替换和医院 传播。然而,很少有研究比较同一人群和时期内同一病毒的临床和社区采样,因此尚不清楚临床衍生的序列是否代表社区中传播的病毒。这项研究的附加值据我们所知,这是第一项比较同一地区和重叠时间段内三种呼吸道病毒的临床和社区采样之间的病毒多样性的研究。使用来自华盛顿州社区 监测 研究和州临床 监测 的 10,000 多个完整 基因组,我们发现 RSV 和流感来源之间的进化枝比例和动态相似,但 SARS-CoV-2 不同。在更精细的遗传分辨率下,临床 SARS-CoV-2 序列比群落序列形成更多样化的簇,并且与单克隆抗体耐药性相关的几个尖峰 突变 在群落样本中更为普遍。所有可用证据的含义对于季节性呼吸道病毒,对寻求护理的人进行采样似乎可以捕获社区中传播的大部分多样性,这可能使资源有限的 监测 项目能够依赖临床标本。与具有一定免疫力的人群中的季节性循环相反,在大流行水平的传播期间,当很大程度上易感人群中的大量人在短时间内被感染时,临床和社区样本不可互换,并且仅对临床样本进行测序的程序存在缺失社区中传播的变异的风险,包括与抗病毒药物和单克隆抗体耐药性相关的突变。这些差异可能部分反映了可用的 SARS-CoV-2 基因组 数量大得多,以及大流行期间多种变体的异质混合和共同循环。因此,监测 计划应结合临床和社区抽样,未来的研究应测试这些模式是否适用于其他地区、季节和病原体。

title: An enhanced electrochemiluminescence immunosensor based on PtCo/UiO-66-NH2@luminol for highly sensitive detection of recombinant RSV F protein.
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants and young children. The development of sensitive and reliable methods for the detection of RSV proteins is therefore of great significance for disease prevention and control. In this study, a sandwich-type electrochemiluminescence (ECL) biosensor was developed for the highly sensitive detection of recombinant RSV F protein. A glassy carbon electrode (GCE) was modified with gold nanoparticles (Au NPs) to leverage their excellent conductivity and biocompatibility. The Au NPs not only facilitated electron transfer at the electrode interface but also provided a stable platform for immobilizing the capture antibody (Ab 1 ). The immunosensor was fabricated by sequentially assembling chitosan and Ab 1 on the Au NPs/GCE, blocking with BSA, capturing RSV F protein, and introducing an Ab 2 /PtCo/UiO-66-NH 2 @luminol probe, with Ab 1 immobilized by physical adsorption. A multifunctional PtCo/UiO-66-NH 2 nanocomposite was further designed, with PtCo providing peroxidase-like catalytic activity and UiO-66-NH 2 supplying abundant adsorption sites and amino functional groups. This composite enabled efficient stepwise loading of luminol molecules and detection antibodies (Ab 2 ), thereby achieving cascaded amplification of ECL signals in an H 2 O 2 coreactant system. In the presence of recombinant RSV F protein, a stable "electrode-Ab 1 -RSV F protein-Ab 2 -probe" sandwich complex was formed. Under optimized conditions, the ECL intensity showed a good linear relationship with recombinant RSV F protein concentration in the range of 0.1 pg mL -1 to 10 ng mL -1 , with a calculated detection limit of 0.025 pg mL -1 , experimentally verified at this concentration (n = 6). The proposed biosensor exhibited excellent stability, specificity, and reproducibility, providing a sensitive and reliable proof-of-concept platform for the detection of recombinant RSV F protein, which may serve as a foundation for future clinical validation.

source_records.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants and young children. The development of sensitive and reliable methods for the detection of RSV proteins is therefore of great significance for disease prevention and control. In this study, a sandwich-type electrochemiluminescence (ECL) biosensor was developed for the highly sensitive detection of recombinant RSV F protein. A glassy carbon electrode (GCE) was modified with gold nanoparticles (Au NPs) to leverage their excellent conductivity and biocompatibility. The Au NPs not only facilitated electron transfer at the electrode interface but also provided a stable platform for immobilizing the capture antibody (Ab 1 ). The immunosensor was fabricated by sequentially assembling chitosan and Ab 1 on the Au NPs/GCE, blocking with BSA, capturing RSV F protein, and introducing an Ab 2 /PtCo/UiO-66-NH 2 @luminol probe, with Ab 1 immobilized by physical adsorption. A multifunctional PtCo/UiO-66-NH 2 nanocomposite was further designed, with PtCo providing peroxidase-like catalytic activity and UiO-66-NH 2 supplying abundant adsorption sites and amino functional groups. This composite enabled efficient stepwise loading of luminol molecules and detection antibodies (Ab 2 ), thereby achieving cascaded amplification of ECL signals in an H 2 O 2 coreactant system. In the presence of recombinant RSV F protein, a stable "electrode-Ab 1 -RSV F protein-Ab 2 -probe" sandwich complex was formed. Under optimized conditions, the ECL intensity showed a good linear relationship with recombinant RSV F protein concentration in the range of 0.1 pg mL -1 to 10 ng mL -1 , with a calculated detection limit of 0.025 pg mL -1 , experimentally verified at this concentration (n = 6). The proposed biosensor exhibited excellent stability, specificity, and reproducibility, providing a sensitive and reliable proof-of-concept platform for the detection of recombinant RSV F protein, which may serve as a foundation for future clinical validation.

abstract_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 会导致婴儿和幼儿严重的下呼吸道感染。因此,开发灵敏、可靠的RSV蛋白检测方法对于疾病预防和控制具有重要意义。在本研究中,开发了一种夹心型电化学发光(ECL)生物传感器,用于高灵敏度检测重组RSV F蛋白。用金纳米粒子 (Au NP) 修饰玻碳电极 (GCE),以利用其优异的导电性和生物相容性。Au NP 不仅促进了电极界面上的电子转移,而且还为固定捕获抗体 (Ab 1 ) 提供了稳定的平台。该免疫传感器的制备方法是将壳聚糖和 Ab 1 依次组装在 Au NPs/GCE 上,用 BSA 封闭,捕获 RSV F 蛋白,并引入 Ab 2 /PtCo/UiO-66-NH 2 @luminol 探针,并通过物理吸附固定 Ab 1。进一步设计了多功能PtCo/UiO-66-NH 2 纳米复合材料,其中PtCo提供类似过氧化物酶的催化活性,UiO-66-NH 2 提供丰富的吸附位点和氨基官能团。该复合材料能够有效地逐步加载鲁米诺分子和检测抗体(Ab 2 ),从而在H 2 O 2 共反应体系中实现ECL信号的级联放大。在重组RSV F蛋白存在下,形成稳定的“电极-Ab 1 -RSV F蛋白-Ab 2 -探针”夹心复合物。在优化条件下,ECL强度与重组RSV F蛋白浓度在0.1 pg mL -1 至10 ng mL -1 范围内表现出良好的线性关系,计算检测限为0.025 pg mL -1,经该浓度实验验证(n = 6)。所提出的生物传感器表现出优异的稳定性、特异性和重现性,为重组RSV F蛋白的检测提供了灵敏且可靠的概念验证平台,可作为未来临床验证的基础。

title: Hospital burden, clinical severity, and economic impact of respiratory viral infections in Spain: A population-based study using hospital data (2019-2023).
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Respiratory viral infections are a major cause of hospitalization, morbidity, mortality, and healthcare resource use in Spain. Although influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) account for most of the healthcare burden, the contribution of other respiratory viruses has been less studied. This study aimed to analyze the hospital burden, clinical severity, and economic impact of these infections during the 2019-2023 period. METHODS: A retrospective population-based study was conducted using the Spanish Minimum Basic Data Set (CMBD), including hospitalizations with a diagnosis of respiratory viral infection between 2019 and 2023. Influenza, RSV, adenovirus, metapneumovirus, parainfluenza, and rhinovirus were analyzed. RESULTS: A total of 154,753 hospitalizations were included (mean age: 39 years; 48.6% female). Influenza and RSV accounted for most hospitalizations and total costs. A marked reduction in hospitalizations was observed in 2021, followed by recovery in 2022-2023. RSV, metapneumovirus, rhinovirus, and adenovirus predominantly affected the pediatric population, whereas influenza and parainfluenza had a greater impact on older adults. Overall, 6.5% of patients required ICU admission and in-hospital mortality was 2.7%, highest for influenza (4.2%). Metapneumovirus and rhinovirus showed the highest ICU admission rates. Mean hospital stay was 6.1 days (7.4 days in ICU). Although influenza and RSV generated the highest total costs, other viruses showed higher costs per episode. CONCLUSIONS: Respiratory viral infections impose a substantial healthcare and economic burden, with variable impact according to virus type and age group, highlighting the need for integrated surveillance, prevention, and healthcare planning strategies.

Although influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) account for most of the healthcare burden, the contribution of other respiratory viruses has been less studied. This study aimed to analyze the hospital burden, clinical severity, and economic impact of these infections during the 2019-2023 period. Methods A retrospective population-based study was conducted using the Spanish Minimum Basic Data Set (CMBD), including hospitalizations with a diagnosis of respiratory viral infection between 2019 and 2023. Influenza, RSV, adenovirus, metapneumovirus, parainfluenza, and rhinovirus were analyzed. Results A total of 154,753 hospitalizations were included (mean age: 39 years; 48.6% female). Influenza and RSV accounted for most hospitalizations and total costs. A marked reduction in hospitalizations was observed in 2021, followed by recovery in 2022-2023. RSV, metapneumovirus, rhinovirus, and adenovirus predominantly affected the pediatric population, whereas influenza and parainfluenza had a greater impact on older adults. Overall, 6.5% of patients required ICU admission and in-hospital mortality was 2.7%, highest for influenza (4.2%). Metapneumovirus and rhinovirus showed the highest ICU admission rates. Mean hospital stay was 6.1 days (7.4 days in ICU). Although influenza and RSV generated the highest total costs, other viruses showed higher costs per episode. Conclusions Respiratory viral infections impose a substantial healthcare and economic burden, with variable impact according to virus type and age group, highlighting the need for integrated surveillance, prevention, and healthcare planning strategies.

abstract_zh: 简介:呼吸道病毒感染是西班牙住院、发病、死亡率 和医疗资源使用的主要原因。尽管流感和 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 造成了大部分医疗负担,但其他呼吸道病毒的贡献却很少被研究。本研究旨在分析 2019-2023 年期间这些感染的医院负担、临床严重程度和经济影响。方法:使用西班牙最低基本数据集 (CMBD) 进行一项基于人群的回顾性研究,包括 2019 年至 2023 年间因呼吸道病毒感染 诊断 住院的情况。分析了流感、RSV、腺病毒、偏肺病毒、副流感和鼻病毒。结果:总共纳入了 154,753 名住院患者(平均年龄:39 岁;48.6% 为女性)。流感和呼吸道合胞病毒占住院治疗和总费用的大部分。2021 年住院人数显着减少,随后在 2022-2023 年恢复。RSV、偏肺病毒、鼻病毒和腺病毒主要影响儿童群体,而流感和副流感对老年人的影响更大。总体而言,6.5% 的患者需要入住 ICU,住院 死亡率 为 2.7%,其中流感患者最高(4.2%)。偏肺病毒和鼻病毒的 ICU 入住率最高。平均住院时间为 6.1 天(ICU 住院时间为 7.4 天)。尽管流感和呼吸道合胞病毒产生的总成本最高,但其他病毒每次发作的成本更高。结论:呼吸道病毒感染造成了巨大的医疗保健和经济负担,根据病毒类型和年龄组的不同,其影响也各不相同,这凸显了综合 监测、预防和医疗保健规划策略的必要性。

title: Three-Year Polymerase Chain Reaction-Based Surveillance of Respiratory Tract Infections in Adults and Seasonal Patterns.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the aetiological composition, seasonal variation and risk factors of adult respiratory tract infections in Ganzhou, Jiangxi Province, during 2023-2025. METHODS: A total of 8,493 adults (≥18 years) with respiratory symptoms were enrolled from a tertiary hospital during 2023-2025. Oropharyngeal and nasopharyngeal swabs were tested using multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) panels targeting six categories of seven respiratory pathogens: influenza A and B viruses, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), parainfluenza virus types I and III, adenovirus and Mycoplasma pneumoniae. Mixed infections (two or more pathogens) were reported separately. Data were analysed by univariate analysis and multivariate logistic regression. RESULTS: The overall pathogen detection rate was 4.14% (352/8,493), comprising 325 single infections (92.33%) and 27 mixed infections (7.67%). Among single infections, M. pneumoniae (39.69%), influenza A virus (28.00%) and RSV (16.00%) predominated. Infections peaked in winter-spring (December-March). Age ≥65 years (OR = 2.35, 95% CI: 1.78-3.09), underlying diseases (OR = 2.41, 95% CI: 1.89-3.08) and emergency department admission (OR = 1.58, 95% CI: 1.24-2.01) were independent risk factors. CONCLUSION: Adult respiratory infections in Ganzhou show clear winter-spring seasonality, with M. pneumoniae, influenza A virus and RSV as leading pathogens. These findings support seasonally targeted surveillance - with enhanced monitoring for M. pneumoniae and influenza during winter-spring months - and prioritised vaccination, expanded diagnostic panels and early PCR-based diagnosis for adults aged ≥65 years and those with underlying diseases, thereby strengthening local respiratory infection prevention and control strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a three-year polymerase chain reaction-based surveillance of respiratory tract infections in adults in Ganzhou, Jiangxi Province, during 2023-2025. It aimed to understand the aetiological composition, seasonal variation and risk factors of these infections. The study enrolled 8,493 adults with respiratory symptoms and tested oropharyngeal and nasopharyngeal swabs using multiplex real-time PCR panels targeting seven respiratory pathogens, including respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). The overall pathogen detection rate was 4.14%, with RSV accounting for 16% of single infections. Infections peaked in winter-spring, and age ≥65 years, underlying diseases and emergency department admission were identified as independent risk factors. The findings suggest that RSV has a significant seasonal pattern and highlight the need for targeted surveillance and early diagnosis in high-risk groups. The study is based on abstract-only evidence and has moderate strength due to its observational design and limited scope.

title: Viral Infections and Dysregulation of Neurotrophin Signaling: Potential impact in the Central Nervous System.
abstract: Viral infections can perturb neurotrophin signaling in the central nervous system, with important consequences for neuronal survival, synaptic plasticity, neurodevelopment, and long-term cognitive and neuropsychiatric outcomes. Neurotrophins, including nerve growth factor, brain-derived neurotrophic factor, neurotrophin-3, and neurotrophin-4, mediate their actions primarily through tropomyosin receptor kinases (TrkA, TrkB and TrkC) and the p75 neurotrophin receptor (p75NTR), activating intracellular pathways such as PI3K-AKT, MAPK-ERK, and PLC-γ. Growing evidence suggests that both neurotropic/neuroinvasive and non-classically neurotropic viruses can interfere with these pathways through multiple mechanisms, including those elicited by direct infection of neural and glial cells, interference with endosomal trafficking required for sustained Trk signaling, and inflammation-driven alterations in neurotrophin expression and receptor balance. This review summarizes current knowledge on how selected viruses affect neurotrophin availability and downstream signaling in experimental models and clinical settings. Specifically, the review focuses on: 1) viruses capable of establishing life-long latent or persistent infection such as i) herpesviruses (herpes simplex virus-1; Epstein Barr virus; human cytomegalovirus), and ii) human immunodeficiency virus; 2) other neurotropic viruses driving peculiar neuropathological profiles, such West Nile virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, Zika virus, and Borna disease virus 1; 3) respiratory viruses, such as influenza A virus, human respiratory syncytial virus, and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2. For each virus group, we discuss convergent pathogenic mechanisms and receptor-level interference with neurotrophin signaling. We further highlight some gaps in current knowledge, including limited longitudinal human data and the underexplored role of viral co-infections and reactivations, and the unclear causal directionality of neurotrophin dysregulation.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the impact of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) on neurotrophin signaling in the central nervous system. It highlights how RSV can disrupt these pathways through direct infection of neural and glial cells, interference with endosomal trafficking, and inflammation-driven changes in neurotrophin expression and receptor balance. The review also identifies key gaps in knowledge, including limited longitudinal human data and the unclear causal directionality of neurotrophin dysregulation. These findings underscore the need for further research to better understand the long-term neurological consequences of RSV infection and to explore the role of co-infections and reactivations in this context.

abstract_zh: 病毒感染会扰乱中枢神经系统中的神经营养素信号传导,对神经元存活、突触可塑性、神经发育以及长期认知和神经精神结果产生重要影响。神经营养蛋白,包括神经生长因子、脑源性神经营养因子、神经营养蛋白-3 和神经营养蛋白-4,主要通过原肌球蛋白受体激酶(TrkA、TrkB 和 TrkC)和 p75 神经营养蛋白受体 (p75NTR) 介导其作用,激活细胞内通路,例如 PI3K-AKT、MAPK-ERK 和 PLC-γ。越来越多的证据表明,嗜神经/神经侵袭性病毒和非经典嗜神经病毒都可以通过多种机制干扰这些途径,包括直接感染神经和胶质细胞引起的机制、干扰持续 Trk 信号传导所需的内体运输以及炎症驱动的神经营养蛋白表达和受体平衡的改变。这篇综述总结了有关选定病毒如何影响实验模型和临床环境中神经营养蛋白可用性和下游信号传导的当前知识。具体而言,该审查重点关注:1)能够建立终生潜伏或持续感染的病毒,例如i)疱疹病毒(单纯疱疹病毒-1;Epstein Barr病毒;人类巨细胞病毒)和ii)人类免疫缺陷病毒;2)其他导致特殊神经病理学特征的嗜神经病毒,例如西尼罗河病毒、日本脑炎病毒、寨卡病毒和博尔纳病病毒1;3)呼吸道病毒,例如甲型流感病毒、人类呼吸道合胞病毒和严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2。对于每个病毒组,我们讨论了趋同的致病机制和受体水平对神经营养蛋白信号传导的干扰。我们进一步强调了当前知识中的一些差距,包括有限的纵向人类数据和病毒共同感染和再激活的作用尚未充分探索,以及神经营养蛋白失调的因果方向性尚不清楚。

title: Nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV hospitalizations in children 8-23 months at risk of severe RSV
abstract: Importance: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of hospitalization in high-risk young children during their second RSV season. Nirsevimab, a long-acting monoclonal antibody against RSV, is recommended for some children who are at increased risk for severe RSV and entering their second RSV season to prevent severe RSV disease. Because of limited eligibility criteria for second season nirsevimab, estimating its effectiveness is challenging. Objective: We evaluated nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalizations among young children eligible to receive nirsevimab during their second RSV season. Design: This retrospective case control study with a test-negative design was conducted during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 RSV seasons. Setting: Enrollment was in 26 hospitals across 24 U.S. Participants: Children eligible for nirsevimab during their second RSV season (as recommended in August 2023) were included. Nirsevimab-eligible children 8-23 months old hospitalized with respiratory symptoms were enrolled. Case-patients tested positive for RSV; control-patients tested negative for RSV. Exposures: Receipt of nirsevimab before or during the second RSV season and at least 7 days before symptom onset. Outcomes and measures: RSV-associated hospitalization. We estimated nirsevimab effectiveness using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, month and year of hospitalization, census region, and sex comparing the odds of second season nirsevimab receipt among case- and control-patients. Results: One hundred six case-patients and 125 control-patients were analyzed. Distributions of age, sex, race and ethnicity, and region were similar in case- and control-patients. Most case- and control-patients were eligible for nirsevimab because of chronic lung disease of prematurity (84.0% and 69.6%, respectively). Overall, 21 (19.8%) of case-patients and 53 (42.4%) of control-patients received nirsevimab. Adjusted nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalizations was 78.1% (95% CI, 55.2%-89.3%); the median interval from nirsevimab receipt to symptom onset was 66.5 days (IQR = 30-96 days). Effectiveness was estimated to be higher if nirsevimab was received 8-59 days before symptom onset (88.5%, 95% CI, 63.4%-96.4%). Conclusions: This analysis provides real-world estimates of substantial nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalizations for high-risk U.S. children in their second RSV season These data support recommendations for nirsevimab as a preventive strategy in this population.

title_zh: 尼塞韦单抗 对有严重 RSV 风险的 8-23 个月儿童 RSV 住院治疗的有效性
source_body_en: Importance: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of hospitalization in high-risk young children during their second RSV season. Nirsevimab, a long-acting monoclonal antibody against RSV, is recommended for some children who are at increased risk for severe RSV and entering their second RSV season to prevent severe RSV disease. Because of limited eligibility criteria for second season nirsevimab, estimating its effectiveness is challenging. Objective: We evaluated nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalizations among young children eligible to receive nirsevimab during their second RSV season. Design: This retrospective case control study with a test-negative design was conducted during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 RSV seasons. Setting: Enrollment was in 26 hospitals across 24 U.S. Participants: Children eligible for nirsevimab during their second RSV season (as recommended in August 2023) were included. Nirsevimab-eligible children 8-23 months old hospitalized with respiratory symptoms were enrolled. Case-patients tested positive for RSV; control-patients tested negative for RSV. Exposures: Receipt of nirsevimab before or during the second RSV season and at least 7 days before symptom onset. Outcomes and measures: RSV-associated hospitalization. We estimated nirsevimab effectiveness using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, month and year of hospitalization, census region, and sex comparing the odds of second season nirsevimab receipt among case- and control-patients. Results: One hundred six case-patients and 125 control-patients were analyzed. Distributions of age, sex, race and ethnicity, and region were similar in case- and control-patients. Most case- and control-patients were eligible for nirsevimab because of chronic lung disease of prematurity (84.0% and 69.6%, respectively). Overall, 21 (19.8%) of case-patients and 53 (42.4%) of control-patients received nirsevimab. Adjusted nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalizations was 78.1% (95% CI, 55.2%-89.3%); the median interval from nirsevimab receipt to symptom onset was 66.5 days (IQR = 30-96 days). Effectiveness was estimated to be higher if nirsevimab was received 8-59 days before symptom onset (88.5%, 95% CI, 63.4%-96.4%). Conclusions: This analysis provides real-world estimates of substantial nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalizations for high-risk U.S. children in their second RSV season These data support recommendations for nirsevimab as a preventive strategy in this population.

title: Influenza A/B, RSV and SARS-CoV-2 Co-Detection Among Adults with Acute Respiratory Illness in Zimbabwe, 2022–2023: A Sub-Study of a COVID-19 Vaccine Effectiveness Study
abstract: Background: /Objectives: Influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) cause overlapping respiratory illness, but Zimbabwean adult multipathogen data remain limited. We described influenza and RSV detection and co-detection with SARS-CoV-2 among adults enrolled in the ZIMCOVVAR study. Methods: This retrospective sub-study included nasopharyngeal specimens from adults with acute respiratory illness recruited in six Zimbabwean provinces during 2022-2023. Following exclusion of duplicate and unlinked records, 1,429 participants were analyzed. Influenza A, influenza B, and RSV were tested by multiplex real-time reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (PCR); recorded target cycle thresholds (Ct) ≤30 were provisionally classified as signals. Valid target-specific denominators remained unresolved. Proportions, confidence intervals, monthly patterns, and associations with SARS-CoV-2 status were examined. Results: The analytic cohort comprised 281 SARS-CoV-2-positive and 1,148 negative participants; median age was 35 years and 68.2% were female. Ct-defined influenza A, RSV, and influenza B signals occurred in 191/1,429 (13.4%), 53/1,429 (3.7%), and 2/1,429 (0.1%), respectively. Influenza A was recorded in 68/281 (24.2%) SARS-CoV-2-positive versus 123/1,148 (10.7%) negative participants. RSV was recorded in 3/281 (1.1%) versus 50/1,148 (4.4%), respectively. These are provisional signals per linked record, not valid-result positivity estimates; testing-group exclusion reversed the adjusted association. Conclusions: The selected adult cohort showed recorded influenza and RSV detections alongside SARS-CoV-2, supporting continued investigation of multiple respiratory pathogens in symptomatic adults. The findings require cautious interpretation because of nonrepresentative sampling and unresolved testing-group effects; quality-assured, multi-season surveillance is needed to inform local prevention planning.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed co-detection of influenza A, influenza B, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) with SARS-CoV-2 among adults with acute respiratory illness in Zimbabwe during 2022–2023. The research aimed to address limited data on multipathogen respiratory illnesses in the region. Using multiplex real-time reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (PCR), the study found that RSV was detected in 3.7% of specimens, with a higher proportion in SARS-CoV-2-positive participants. The results suggest potential co-circulation of these viruses, but the findings are provisional due to unresolved testing-group effects and nonrepresentative sampling. The study highlights the need for quality-assured, multi-season surveillance to better understand the epidemiology of respiratory pathogens and inform local prevention strategies.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们描述了参加 ZIMCOVVAR 研究的成年人中流感和 RSV 的检测以及与 SARS-CoV-2 的共同检测。这项回顾性子研究包括 2022 年至 2023 年在津巴布韦六个省份招募的患有急性呼吸道疾病的成年人的鼻咽标本。

elements_zh.main_results: 分析 队列研究 包括 281 名 SARS-CoV-2 阳性参与者和 1,148 名阴性参与者;中位年龄为 35 岁,其中 68.2% 为女性。Ct 定义的甲型流感、RSV 和乙型流感信号分别出现在 191/1,429 (13.4%)、53/1,429 (3.7%) 和 2/1,429 (0.1%) 中。68/281 (24.2%) SARS-CoV-2 阳性参与者记录了甲型流感,而 123/1,148 (10.7%) 阴性参与者记录了甲型流感。RSV 记录分别为 3/281 (1.1%) 和 50/1,148 (4.4%)。

Methods: This retrospective sub-study included nasopharyngeal specimens from adults with acute respiratory illness recruited in six Zimbabwean provinces during 2022-2023. Following exclusion of duplicate and unlinked records, 1,429 participants were analyzed. Influenza A, influenza B, and RSV were tested by multiplex real-time reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (PCR); recorded target cycle thresholds (Ct) ≤30 were provisionally classified as signals. Valid target-specific denominators remained unresolved. Proportions, confidence intervals, monthly patterns, and associations with SARS-CoV-2 status were examined. Results: The analytic cohort comprised 281 SARS-CoV-2-positive and 1,148 negative participants; median age was 35 years and 68.2% were female. Ct-defined influenza A, RSV, and influenza B signals occurred in 191/1,429 (13.4%), 53/1,429 (3.7%), and 2/1,429 (0.1%), respectively. Influenza A was recorded in 68/281 (24.2%) SARS-CoV-2-positive versus 123/1,148 (10.7%) negative participants. RSV was recorded in 3/281 (1.1%) versus 50/1,148 (4.4%), respectively. These are provisional signals per linked record, not valid-result positivity estimates; testing-group exclusion reversed the adjusted association. Conclusions: The selected adult cohort showed recorded influenza and RSV detections alongside SARS-CoV-2, supporting continued investigation of multiple respiratory pathogens in symptomatic adults. The findings require cautious interpretation because of nonrepresentative sampling and unresolved testing-group effects; quality-assured, multi-season surveillance is needed to inform local prevention planning.
abstract_zh: 背景:/目标:流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2 (SARS-CoV-2) 会引起重叠的呼吸道疾病,但津巴布韦成人多病原体数据仍然有限。我们描述了参加 ZIMCOVVAR 研究的成年人中流感和 RSV 的检测以及与 SARS-CoV-2 的共同检测。方法:这项回顾性子研究包括 2022 年至 2023 年在津巴布韦六个省份招募的患有急性呼吸道疾病的成年人的鼻咽标本。排除重复和未关联的记录后,对 1,429 名参与者进行了分析。通过多重实时逆转录聚合酶链反应 (PCR) 检测甲型流感、乙型流感和 RSV;记录的目标周期阈值(Ct)≤30 暂时归类为信号。有效的特定目标分母仍未解决。检查了比例、置信区间、每月模式以及与 SARS-CoV-2 状态的关联。结果:分析 队列研究 包括 281 名 SARS-CoV-2 阳性参与者和 1,148 名阴性参与者;中位年龄为 35 岁,其中 68.2% 为女性。Ct 定义的甲型流感、RSV 和乙型流感信号分别出现在 191/1,429 (13.4%)、53/1,429 (3.7%) 和 2/1,429 (0.1%) 中。68/281 (24.2%) SARS-CoV-2 阳性参与者记录了甲型流感,而 123/1,148 (10.7%) 阴性参与者记录了甲型流感。RSV 记录分别为 3/281 (1.1%) 和 50/1,148 (4.4%)。这些是每个链接记录的临时信号,不是有效结果的积极性估计;测试组排除逆转了调整后的关联。结论:选定的成人 队列研究 显示记录的流感和 RSV 检测以及 SARS-CoV-2,支持对有症状成人中的多种呼吸道病原体的继续研究。由于抽样不具代表性且测试组效应尚未解决,研究结果需要谨慎解释;需要有质量保证的多季节 监测 来为当地预防规划提供信息。

title: Comparison of Dissemination of Aerosol and Splatter during Ultrasonic Scaling using Different Masks: A Pilot Study with Relevance to Respiratory Infection Transmission
abstract: Abstract Background: Dentists are routinely exposed to a high amount of micro-organism load due to primarily being responsible for the treatment of the structures if the mouth – which is a well-known source of huge bacterial loads. Also, as COVID-19 recently affected the entire world, masks thus were considered to act as a comprehensive strategy of measures to suppress transmission. However, the relevance of aerosol and respiratory infection control extends beyond COVID-19, as respiratory pathogens including seasonal influenza viruses such as influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, commonly referred to as swine flu, influenza A(H3N2), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and other respiratory viruses continue to circulate and may be transmitted through respiratory particles. Aim: To compare the dissemination of aerosol and splatter during ultrasonic scaling using different masks. Method: In this study we evaluated the dissemination of four masks that is N-95 with respirator, N-95 without respirator, a combination of cloth mask and N-95 without respirator, and normal surgical mask by calculating the surface are of filter paper with the help of a previously marked scale which was divided into one-centimeter squares. Results: Best protection was seen to be offered by the combined use of the double masking – N-95 without filter plus cloth mask, followed by N-95 mask alone and then the surgical mask.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the need for effective infection control measures in dental settings, where dentists are routinely exposed to high microbial loads. The background highlights the relevance of aerosol and respiratory infection control beyond the context of COVID-19, as respiratory pathogens such as respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) continue to circulate and may be transmitted through respiratory particles.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This pilot study evaluated the dissemination of aerosol and splatter during ultrasonic scaling using different masks. The study was conducted in a dental setting, and the participants were dentists involved in the procedure.
analysis.methods: The study compared the effectiveness of four masks: N-95 with respirator, N-95 without respirator, a combination of cloth mask and N-95 without respirator, and normal surgical mask. The surface area of filter paper was calculated using a previously marked scale divided into one-centimeter squares to assess the dissemination of aerosol and splatter.
analysis.main_results: The results indicated that the best protection was provided by the combined use of double masking – N-95 without filter plus cloth mask, followed by the N-95 mask alone, and then the surgical mask.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that double masking offers superior protection against aerosol dissemination during dental procedures. This is a novel approach to infection control in settings where respiratory pathogens are a concern.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have specific implications for improving infection control strategies in dental environments, particularly in reducing the transmission of respiratory pathogens such as respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a pilot study, which limits the generalizability of the results. The evidence is based on a single method of assessing aerosol dissemination, which may not fully capture the complexity of pathogen transmission in real-world scenarios.

analysis.summary_en: This pilot study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of different masks in preventing aerosol and splatter dissemination during ultrasonic scaling in dental settings. The study highlighted the importance of infection control measures, particularly in environments where respiratory pathogens like RSV are prevalent. The results showed that combining an N-95 mask without a filter with a cloth mask provided the best protection. The authors interpreted these findings as a novel approach to reducing pathogen transmission in dental procedures. The study's implications for public health include the potential for improved infection control strategies in dental practices. However, the study's limitations include its small scale and reliance on a single method of assessment, which may affect the strength of the evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决牙科环境中有效感染控制措施的需求,因为牙医经常暴露在高微生物负荷下。背景强调了在 COVID-19 背景下气溶胶和呼吸道感染控制的相关性,因为 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 等呼吸道病原体继续循环,并可能通过呼吸道颗粒传播。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该试点研究评估了使用不同面罩进行超声洁牙期间气溶胶和飞溅的传播情况。该研究是在牙科环境中进行的,参与者是参与该手术的牙医。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究比较了四种口罩的有效性:带呼吸器的 N-95、不带呼吸器的 N-95、布口罩和不带呼吸器的 N-95 的组合以及普通外科口罩。使用先前标记的一厘米见方的刻度来计算滤纸的表面积,以评估气溶胶和飞溅的传播。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果表明,双重口罩的组合使用提供了最好的保护——无过滤器的N-95加布口罩,其次是单独的N-95口罩,然后是外科口罩。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明双重遮蔽在牙科手术过程中提供了针对气溶胶传播的卓越保护。这是一种在呼吸道病原体存在问题的环境中控制感染的新方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现对于改善牙科环境中的感染控制策略具有具体意义,特别是在减少 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 等呼吸道病原体的 传播 方面。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是一项试点研究,限制了结果的普遍性。该证据基于评估气溶胶传播的单一方法,该方法可能无法完全捕捉现实场景中病原体 传播 的复杂性。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the need for effective infection control measures in dental settings, where dentists are routinely exposed to high microbial loads. The background highlights the relevance of aerosol and respiratory infection control beyond the context of COVID-19, as respiratory pathogens such as respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) continue to circulate and may be transmitted through respiratory particles.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This pilot study evaluated the dissemination of aerosol and splatter during ultrasonic scaling using different masks. The study was conducted in a dental setting, and the participants were dentists involved in the procedure.
analysis_en.methods: The study compared the effectiveness of four masks: N-95 with respirator, N-95 without respirator, a combination of cloth mask and N-95 without respirator, and normal surgical mask. The surface area of filter paper was calculated using a previously marked scale divided into one-centimeter squares to assess the dissemination of aerosol and splatter.
analysis_en.main_results: The results indicated that the best protection was provided by the combined use of double masking – N-95 without filter plus cloth mask, followed by the N-95 mask alone, and then the surgical mask.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that double masking offers superior protection against aerosol dissemination during dental procedures. This is a novel approach to infection control in settings where respiratory pathogens are a concern.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have specific implications for improving infection control strategies in dental environments, particularly in reducing the transmission of respiratory pathogens such as respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a pilot study, which limits the generalizability of the results. The evidence is based on a single method of assessing aerosol dissemination, which may not fully capture the complexity of pathogen transmission in real-world scenarios.

title_zh: 使用不同口罩进行超声洁牙期间气溶胶和飞溅传播的比较:与呼吸道感染相关的初步研究 传播
source_body_en: Abstract Background: Dentists are routinely exposed to a high amount of micro-organism load due to primarily being responsible for the treatment of the structures if the mouth – which is a well-known source of huge bacterial loads. Also, as COVID-19 recently affected the entire world, masks thus were considered to act as a comprehensive strategy of measures to suppress transmission. However, the relevance of aerosol and respiratory infection control extends beyond COVID-19, as respiratory pathogens including seasonal influenza viruses such as influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, commonly referred to as swine flu, influenza A(H3N2), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and other respiratory viruses continue to circulate and may be transmitted through respiratory particles. Aim: To compare the dissemination of aerosol and splatter during ultrasonic scaling using different masks. Method: In this study we evaluated the dissemination of four masks that is N-95 with respirator, N-95 without respirator, a combination of cloth mask and N-95 without respirator, and normal surgical mask by calculating the surface are of filter paper with the help of a previously marked scale which was divided into one-centimeter squares. Results: Best protection was seen to be offered by the combined use of the double masking – N-95 without filter plus cloth mask, followed by N-95 mask alone and then the surgical mask.
abstract_zh: 摘要背景:牙医经常暴露在大量的微生物负荷下,因为口腔是众所周知的巨大细菌负荷的来源。此外,由于COVID-19最近影响了全世界,因此口罩被认为是抑制传播的综合措施策略。然而,气溶胶和呼吸道感染控制的相关性超出了 COVID-19 的范围,因为包括季节性流感病毒(例如甲型 H1N1)pdm09 流感(通常称为猪流感)、甲型流感(H3N2)、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和其他呼吸道病毒在内的呼吸道病原体继续循环,并可能通过呼吸道颗粒传播。目的:比较使用不同面罩进行超声洁治时气溶胶和飞溅的传播情况。方法:在本研究中,我们通过预先标记的一厘米见方的刻度尺计算滤纸的表面积,评估了四种口罩的传播情况,即N-95带呼吸器、N-95不带呼吸器、布口罩和N-95不带呼吸器的组合以及普通外科口罩。结果:结合使用双重口罩(无过滤器的 N-95 加布口罩)可提供最佳保护,其次是单独的 N-95 口罩,最后是外科口罩。

title: mRNA-Lipid Nanoparticle Vaccines for Infectious Diseases: Mechanisms of Action and Translational Progress
abstract: Six years after the first emergency use authorizations, mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccines have gone from a platform without a licensed product to one that supplies a large share of the world's COVID-19 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine doses and has completed phase 3 trials for seasonal influenza. Their performance depends on mechanisms that are being resolved with unusual speed at the level of individual cell types, receptors and molecular interactions, and several textbook assumptions have had to be revised in the process. This review follows the vaccine from the formulation vial to the germinal centre. We first describe how the RNA is engineered for efficient translation and for partial escape from cytosolic and endosomal RNA sensors, and why N1-methylpseudouridine is neither immunologically silent nor translationally neutral. We then examine how the ionizable lipid, the helper phospholipid, cholesterol and the PEG-lipid determine particle behaviour, cell uptake and endosomal release, and how the lipid and RNA components act as separable adjuvant signals. Evidence from mouse models and from human lymph node sampling is compared, with attention to the substantial species differences in innate cytokine control that limit extrapolation from mice to people. The clinical section summarizes efficacy and immunogenicity data for COVID-19, RSV and influenza vaccines, and the preclinical and early clinical status of candidates against cytomegalovirus, mpox, HIV, malaria, Nipah virus and Clostridioides difficile. Safety data are discussed in absolute terms rather than as signals alone. We close with the questions that currently block rational improvement: the molecular identity of the lipid sensor, the difficulty of separating immunogenicity from reactogenicity, the absence of a quantitative description of endosomal escape, and the design of antigens for pathogens that do not tolerate a single fixed immunogen.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccines for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), including their mechanisms of action, translational progress, and clinical applications. The central question is how these vaccines function and their potential for broader use in preventing RSV infections.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on evidence from mouse models and human lymph node sampling. It discusses the performance of mRNA-LNP vaccines, emphasizing the need to account for species differences in innate cytokine control when extrapolating findings from mice to humans. The review also outlines the clinical section that summarizes efficacy and immunogenicity data for RSV vaccines and includes preclinical and early clinical status of candidates against other pathogens.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that mRNA-LNP vaccines have transitioned from a platform without a licensed product to one that is widely used for RSV and has completed phase 3 trials for seasonal influenza. It highlights the importance of understanding the molecular mechanisms of vaccine performance, particularly the role of lipid and RNA components in particle behavior, cell uptake, and endosomal release.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies several controversies and evidence gaps, including the molecular identity of the lipid sensor, the difficulty of separating immunogenicity from reactogenicity, the absence of a quantitative description of endosomal escape, and the challenges in designing antigens for pathogens that do not tolerate a single fixed immunogen.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on resolving the molecular identity of the lipid sensor, improving the separation of immunogenicity from reactogenicity, quantifying endosomal escape mechanisms, and developing antigens for pathogens that do not tolerate a single fixed immunogen. These efforts are critical for the rational improvement of mRNA-LNP vaccines.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the development and mechanisms of mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccines for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), highlighting their transition from an unlicensed platform to a major contributor in RSV and influenza vaccine production. The review emphasizes the importance of understanding the molecular interactions between lipid and RNA components, as well as the challenges in translating findings from mouse models to humans due to differences in innate cytokine control. It also outlines key controversies, such as the molecular identity of the lipid sensor and the difficulty of distinguishing immunogenicity from reactogenicity. The review concludes with research and practice implications, suggesting that future efforts should focus on resolving these gaps to improve vaccine design and efficacy for RSV and other pathogens.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 的 mRNA-脂质纳米颗粒 (mRNA-LNP) 疫苗,包括其作用机制、转化进展和临床应用。核心问题是这些 疫苗 如何发挥作用以及它们在预防 RSV 感染方面更广泛应用的潜力。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查基于小鼠模型和人类淋巴结采样的证据。它讨论了 mRNA-LNP 疫苗 的性能,强调在将小鼠的研究结果外推到人类时,需要考虑先天细胞因子控制的物种差异。该综述还概述了临床部分,总结了 RSV 疫苗 的功效和免疫原性数据,并包括候选药物针对其他病原体的临床前和早期临床状态。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,mRNA-LNP 疫苗 已从一个没有许可产品的平台转变为广泛用于 RSV 的平台,并已完成季节性流感的 3 期试验。它强调了了解 疫苗 性能的分子机制的重要性,特别是脂质和 RNA 成分在颗粒行为、细胞摄取和内体释放中的作用。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述指出了一些争议和证据差距,包括脂质传感器的分子身份、区分免疫原性和反应原性的困难、缺乏内体逃逸的定量描述,以及为不耐受单一固定免疫原的病原体设计抗原的挑战。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述表明,未来的研究应集中于解决脂质传感器的分子身份、改善免疫原性与反应原性的分离、量化内体逃逸机制以及开发不耐受单一固定免疫原的病原体的抗原。这些努力对于mRNA-LNP 疫苗的合理改进至关重要。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccines for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), including their mechanisms of action, translational progress, and clinical applications. The central question is how these vaccines function and their potential for broader use in preventing RSV infections.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on evidence from mouse models and human lymph node sampling. It discusses the performance of mRNA-LNP vaccines, emphasizing the need to account for species differences in innate cytokine control when extrapolating findings from mice to humans. The review also outlines the clinical section that summarizes efficacy and immunogenicity data for RSV vaccines and includes preclinical and early clinical status of candidates against other pathogens.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that mRNA-LNP vaccines have transitioned from a platform without a licensed product to one that is widely used for RSV and has completed phase 3 trials for seasonal influenza. It highlights the importance of understanding the molecular mechanisms of vaccine performance, particularly the role of lipid and RNA components in particle behavior, cell uptake, and endosomal release.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies several controversies and evidence gaps, including the molecular identity of the lipid sensor, the difficulty of separating immunogenicity from reactogenicity, the absence of a quantitative description of endosomal escape, and the challenges in designing antigens for pathogens that do not tolerate a single fixed immunogen.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on resolving the molecular identity of the lipid sensor, improving the separation of immunogenicity from reactogenicity, quantifying endosomal escape mechanisms, and developing antigens for pathogens that do not tolerate a single fixed immunogen. These efforts are critical for the rational improvement of mRNA-LNP vaccines.

title_zh: 用于传染病的 mRNA-脂质纳米颗粒 疫苗:作用机制和转化进展
source_body_en: Six years after the first emergency use authorizations, mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccines have gone from a platform without a licensed product to one that supplies a large share of the world's COVID-19 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine doses and has completed phase 3 trials for seasonal influenza. Their performance depends on mechanisms that are being resolved with unusual speed at the level of individual cell types, receptors and molecular interactions, and several textbook assumptions have had to be revised in the process. This review follows the vaccine from the formulation vial to the germinal centre. We first describe how the RNA is engineered for efficient translation and for partial escape from cytosolic and endosomal RNA sensors, and why N1-methylpseudouridine is neither immunologically silent nor translationally neutral. We then examine how the ionizable lipid, the helper phospholipid, cholesterol and the PEG-lipid determine particle behaviour, cell uptake and endosomal release, and how the lipid and RNA components act as separable adjuvant signals. Evidence from mouse models and from human lymph node sampling is compared, with attention to the substantial species differences in innate cytokine control that limit extrapolation from mice to people. The clinical section summarizes efficacy and immunogenicity data for COVID-19, RSV and influenza vaccines, and the preclinical and early clinical status of candidates against cytomegalovirus, mpox, HIV, malaria, Nipah virus and Clostridioides difficile. Safety data are discussed in absolute terms rather than as signals alone. We close with the questions that currently block rational improvement: the molecular identity of the lipid sensor, the difficulty of separating immunogenicity from reactogenicity, the absence of a quantitative description of endosomal escape, and the design of antigens for pathogens that do not tolerate a single fixed immunogen.
abstract_zh: 在首次获得紧急使用授权六年后,mRNA-脂质纳米颗粒 (mRNA-LNP) 疫苗 已从一个没有许可产品的平台转变为供应全球大部分 COVID-19 和 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 疫苗 剂量的平台,并已完成季节性流感的 3 期试验。它们的性能取决于在个体细胞类型、受体和分子相互作用水平上以异常速度解决的机制,并且在此过程中必须修改一些教科书的假设。本次审查遵循 疫苗 从配方瓶到生发中心的整个过程。我们首先描述了如何设计 RNA 以实现有效翻译并部分逃离胞质和内体 RNA 传感器,以及为什么 N1-甲基假尿苷既不是免疫沉默也不是翻译中性。然后,我们研究可电离脂质、辅助磷脂、胆固醇和 PEG-脂质如何决定颗粒行为、细胞摄取和内体释放,以及脂质和 RNA 成分如何充当可分离的佐剂信号。比较了来自小鼠模型和人类淋巴结采样的证据,并注意先天细胞因子控制方面的巨大物种差异,这限制了从小鼠到人类的外推。临床部分总结了 COVID-19、RSV 和流感 疫苗 的功效和免疫原性数据,以及针对巨细胞病毒、mpox、HIV、疟疾、尼帕病毒和艰难梭菌的候选药物的临床前和早期临床状态。安全数据以绝对术语而不是单独作为信号来讨论。我们以目前阻碍合理改进的问题作为结束语:脂质传感器的分子特性、将免疫原性与反应原性分开的困难、缺乏内体逃逸的定量描述以及不耐受单一固定免疫原的病原体的抗原设计。

title: Lagged environmental effects on multi-pathogen respiratory positivity: a distributed-lag nonlinear analysis of seven Sichuan sentinel hospitals, China
abstract: Abstract Acute respiratory infections (ARI) impose a large global burden and show marked seasonality that implicates environmental drivers, yet the lagged effects of these exposures on pathogen-specific positivity remain poorly characterised. Using case-level data from seven sentinel hospitals in Sichuan, China (2024–2026) aggregated to a weekly panel of 23 014 ARI cases, we applied quasi-Poisson distributed-lag non-linear models (cross-basis, 6-week lag; trend spline; city effects; log offset) to estimate cumulative relative risks (90th versus 10th percentile) for temperature, relative humidity and six air pollutants, with within-pathogen false-discovery-rate control. At least one pathogen was detected in 51.9% of cases and co-detection in 18.2%; Haemophilus influenzae and influenza predominated. Relative humidity gave the most stable single-exposure association with respiratory syncytial virus positivity ( RR 2.01, 95% CI 1.06–3.82); it failed FDR control (adjusted P = 0.130 ) and was nullified by temperature co-adjustment ( RR 1.05). influenzae rose with temperature and ozone and fell with PM2.5; SARS-CoV-2 tracked carbon monoxide. Twelve of 40 estimates survived FDR control. The humidity–RSV signal is robust to model specification yet fragile under co-varying exposures — the cautionary lesson — and the reusable output is a transparent screening framework that exposes such fragility, serving exposure science and environmental epidemiology.

title: Current Approaches to Geriatric Immunizat?on: A Narrative Mini-Review
abstract: As the global population ages, the implementation of a "life-course immunization" approach has become a critical pillar for maintaining functional capacity and ensuring healthy aging. Current 2025-2026 guidelines emphasize a strategic transition to trivalent influenza vaccines and the routine administration of novel Respiratory Syncytial Virus vaccines for high-risk geriatric cohorts. Furthermore, clinical protocols prioritize high-dose or adjuvanted formulations to overcome immunosenescence and provide robust protection against invasive pneumococcal disease, herpes zoster, and COVID-19 subvariants. Despite these advancements, significant disparities in vaccine access and public awareness persist, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Strengthening national immunization schedules through the integration of these next-generation vaccines is essential to alleviate the burden on healthcare systems and reduce preventable mortality. Ultimately, the shift toward personalized immunization strategies aims to ensure that every older adult achieves optimal seroprotection and a higher quality of life.
journal: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)

Current 2025-2026 guidelines emphasize a strategic transition to trivalent influenza vaccines and the routine administration of novel Respiratory Syncytial Virus vaccines for high-risk geriatric cohorts. title: Adaptive forecasting and alert evaluation for pediatric RSV and influenza hospitalization burden using public U.S. surveillance data: a time-series study
abstract: Pediatric influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) hospitalization surges strain hospitals and public health agencies. Post-pandemic changes in seasonality and surveillance practice have weakened fixed seasonal baselines. We evaluated whether public surveillance signals can support transparent warning evaluation for pediatric influenza and RSV hospitalization burden. We conducted a retrospective ecological time-series study using aggregated U.S. RESP-NET hospitalization surveillance and related public signal streams from October 2018 through March 2026. Outcomes were weekly pediatric hospitalization rates for influenza and RSV among children aged 0–4 and 5–17 years. We compared a prior-year same-week seasonal naïve baseline with expanding-window ridge models using seasonal/autoregressive terms and feasible public signals, including emergency department (ED) percent-visit indicators. Forecasts were evaluated by rolling-origin validation, with a finalized-data sensitivity excluding the most recent 4 weeks. We summarized mean absolute error (MAE), alert utility, onset lead time, and expected loss under training-quantile alert thresholds. For RSV among children aged 0–4 years, an ED-feasible ridge model improved matched-week forecasts versus the seasonal naïve baseline at horizon 1 under the finalized-data sensitivity (paired MAE improvement 3.49; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.59 to 5.69; paired n = 104). Influenza gains were smaller and uncertain (ages 0–4 years, horizon 1: paired MAE improvement 0.60; 95% CI -0.24 to 1.24; paired n = 51). Direct matched comparisons of autoregressive/seasonal ridge models with versus without ED terms did not show a stable independent ED point-error gain. At a fixed 90th training-quantile alert threshold and miss: false-alarm cost ratio of 2.0, expected-loss ratios relative to the seasonal baseline were 0.280 for RSV ages 0–4 years and 0.545 for influenza ages 0–4 years. These findings support pathogen-specific, locally calibrated strategies for pediatric respiratory-virus hospitalization warning. Adaptive ridge models improved RSV warning metrics relative to a fixed prior-year baseline, whereas ED terms did not improve matched point-error accuracy beyond AR+season terms. ED signals are therefore a feasible syndromic layer for alert-policy evaluation, not evidence of an independent forecasting gain.

title_zh: 使用美国 监测 公开数据对儿科 RSV 和流感住院负担进行自适应预测和警报评估:一项时间序列研究
source_body_en: Pediatric influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) hospitalization surges strain hospitals and public health agencies. Post-pandemic changes in seasonality and surveillance practice have weakened fixed seasonal baselines. We evaluated whether public surveillance signals can support transparent warning evaluation for pediatric influenza and RSV hospitalization burden. We conducted a retrospective ecological time-series study using aggregated U.S. RESP-NET hospitalization surveillance and related public signal streams from October 2018 through March 2026. Outcomes were weekly pediatric hospitalization rates for influenza and RSV among children aged 0–4 and 5–17 years. We compared a prior-year same-week seasonal naïve baseline with expanding-window ridge models using seasonal/autoregressive terms and feasible public signals, including emergency department (ED) percent-visit indicators. Forecasts were evaluated by rolling-origin validation, with a finalized-data sensitivity excluding the most recent 4 weeks. We summarized mean absolute error (MAE), alert utility, onset lead time, and expected loss under training-quantile alert thresholds. For RSV among children aged 0–4 years, an ED-feasible ridge model improved matched-week forecasts versus the seasonal naïve baseline at horizon 1 under the finalized-data sensitivity (paired MAE improvement 3.49; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.59 to 5.69; paired n = 104). Influenza gains were smaller and uncertain (ages 0–4 years, horizon 1: paired MAE improvement 0.60; 95% CI -0.24 to 1.24; paired n = 51). Direct matched comparisons of autoregressive/seasonal ridge models with versus without ED terms did not show a stable independent ED point-error gain. At a fixed 90th training-quantile alert threshold and miss: false-alarm cost ratio of 2.0, expected-loss ratios relative to the seasonal baseline were 0.280 for RSV ages 0–4 years and 0.545 for influenza ages 0–4 years. These findings support pathogen-specific, locally calibrated strategies for pediatric respiratory-virus hospitalization warning. Adaptive ridge models improved RSV warning metrics relative to a fixed prior-year baseline, whereas ED terms did not improve matched point-error accuracy beyond AR+season terms. ED signals are therefore a feasible syndromic layer for alert-policy evaluation, not evidence of an independent forecasting gain.
