title: Does the Effectiveness of the Nirsevimab Immunization Programs Decline from One RSV Season to the Next? Real-World Evidence from Northeastern Italy
abstract: Background: Nirsevimab has demonstrated high effectiveness in preventing severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease in infants. However, real-world evidence from subsequent seasonal immunization campaigns remains limited. We evaluated the effectiveness of universal infant immunization during a second RSV season and assessed protection during the following season after immunization in the previous year. Methods: We conducted a population-based retrospective cohort study in the Province of Udine, Italy, using linked anonymized regional healthcare databases. All infants born between 1 April 2025 and 31 March 2026 were included in the analysis of the 2025–2026 RSV season. RSV-related hospitalizations were identified from hospital discharge diagnoses. Effectiveness was estimated using multivariable logistic regression and a Cox proportional hazards model with time-varying immunization status. We also assessed RSV-related hospitalizations during the subsequent season among infants who had received nirsevimab during the previous campaign. Seasonal hospitalization risks for RSV and other respiratory viral infections were compared across pre- and post-implementation seasons. Results: Of 2620 infants born during the second campaign, 2293 (87.5%) received nirsevimab. Twenty infants were hospitalized for RSV-related conditions, including 13/2293 (5.67 per 1000) immunized and 7/327 (21.41 per 1000) non-immunized infants (p = 0.008). Adjusted analyses showed significantly lower odds and hazard of RSV-related hospitalization among immunized infants (OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.09–0.57; HR 0.27, 95% CI 0.11–0.69), corresponding to estimated effectiveness of 78% and 73%, respectively. During the following RSV season, six infants from the previous birth cohort were hospitalized with RSV-related conditions, all of whom had received nirsevimab during the preceding campaign (cohort coverage: 78.5%). Hospitalization rates for non-RSV respiratory viruses were lower in the two post-implementation seasons than in the preceding seasons, although this ecological analysis was not designed to establish causality. Conclusions: Universal infant immunization with nirsevimab remained highly effective in preventing RSV-related hospitalization during the second seasonal campaign, achieving high population coverage. No evidence of residual protection was observed during the subsequent RSV season after immunization in the previous year. Continued real-world surveillance is warranted to monitor nirsevimab effectiveness and the broader epidemiology of respiratory viral infections following widespread implementation.

source_records.abstract: Background: Nirsevimab has demonstrated high effectiveness in preventing severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease in infants. However, real-world evidence from subsequent seasonal immunization campaigns remains limited. We evaluated the effectiveness of universal infant immunization during a second RSV season and assessed protection during the following season after immunization in the previous year. Methods: We conducted a population-based retrospective cohort study in the Province of Udine, Italy, using linked anonymized regional healthcare databases. All infants born between 1 April 2025 and 31 March 2026 were included in the analysis of the 2025–2026 RSV season. RSV-related hospitalizations were identified from hospital discharge diagnoses. Effectiveness was estimated using multivariable logistic regression and a Cox proportional hazards model with time-varying immunization status. We also assessed RSV-related hospitalizations during the subsequent season among infants who had received nirsevimab during the previous campaign. Seasonal hospitalization risks for RSV and other respiratory viral infections were compared across pre- and post-implementation seasons. Results: Of 2620 infants born during the second campaign, 2293 (87.5%) received nirsevimab. Twenty infants were hospitalized for RSV-related conditions, including 13/2293 (5.67 per 1000) immunized and 7/327 (21.41 per 1000) non-immunized infants (p = 0.008). Adjusted analyses showed significantly lower odds and hazard of RSV-related hospitalization among immunized infants (OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.09–0.57; HR 0.27, 95% CI 0.11–0.69), corresponding to estimated effectiveness of 78% and 73%, respectively. During the following RSV season, six infants from the previous birth cohort were hospitalized with RSV-related conditions, all of whom had received nirsevimab during the preceding campaign (cohort coverage: 78.5%). Hospitalization rates for non-RSV respiratory viruses were lower in the two post-implementation seasons than in the preceding seasons, although this ecological analysis was not designed to establish causality. Conclusions: Universal infant immunization with nirsevimab remained highly effective in preventing RSV-related hospitalization during the second seasonal campaign, achieving high population coverage. No evidence of residual protection was observed during the subsequent RSV season after immunization in the previous year. Continued real-world surveillance is warranted to monitor nirsevimab effectiveness and the broader epidemiology of respiratory viral infections following widespread implementation.

title: Impact of expanding nirsevimab immunoprophylaxis, extended window and catch-up, on RSV hospitalizations in infants: a three-season, multicentre, population-based study in Emilia-Romagna, Italy
abstract: Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of hospitalization in infancy, particularly during the first months of life. Nirsevimab has substantially reduced RSV-related hospitalizations in early real-world studies, but the incremental population-level benefit of expanding an established seasonal programme to broader birth cohorts remains uncertain. In Emilia-Romagna, Italy, nirsevimab was introduced for the 2024–25 RSV season as seasonal at-birth immunoprophylaxis and expanded in 2025–26 to include at-birth immunoprophylaxis for infants born from August 2025 through March 2026 and catch-up immunization for infants born from April through July 2025. We assessed whether this expanded strategy provided an additional reduction in RSV-compatible hospitalizations. Methods We conducted a multicentre, population-based observational before–after study using hospital discharge records from eleven centres, covering approximately 69% of hospitalizations among infants aged <12 months. RSV-compatible hospitalizations were compared across three seasons: Pre-Nirsevimab (2023–24), Seasonal (2024–25), and Extended seasonal + catch-up (2025–26). Incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were estimated by negative binomial regression adjusted for sex and age. Net avoided hospitalizations were also calculated. Results Age-standardized RSV-compatible hospitalization rates declined from 21.9 per 100, 000 person-days in 2023–24 to 10.1 in 2024–25 and 7.8 in 2025–26. Compared with the Seasonal strategy, the Extended seasonal + catch-up strategy was associated with a further 22% reduction in hospitalization risk (IRR 0.78; 95% CI 0.69–0.88; p<0.001) and a 64% reduction versus Pre-Nirsevimab (IRR 0.36; 95% CI 0.31–0.42). An estimated 103.3 additional hospitalizations were avoided versus 2024–25 and 677.8 versus Pre-Nirsevimab, corresponding to approximately 52 and 339 avoided hospitalizations per 10, 000 infants, respectively. Findings were consistent in infants aged 0–180 days. Conclusions Expanding nirsevimab immunoprophylaxis was associated with a further significant reduction in RSV-compatible hospitalizations beyond that achieved with seasonal-only administration. Given the observational design, causal inference should remain cautious.

Methods We conducted a multicentre, population-based observational before–after study using hospital discharge records from eleven centres, covering approximately 69% of hospitalizations among infants aged <12 months. Conclusions Expanding nirsevimab immunoprophylaxis was associated with a further significant reduction in RSV-compatible hospitalizations beyond that achieved with seasonal-only administration. title: Pathogen spectrum and its association with hospital length of stay in 112 pathogen-tested children with bronchiolitis: a retrospective study from a cohort of 132 hospitalized cases in Hebei Children's Hospital
abstract: Objective To investigate the pathogen spectrum and epidemiological characteristics of hospitalized children with bronchiolitis admitted to Hebei Children's Hospital, and to analyze the relationship between different pathogens or mixed infections and clinical recovery speed, providing a clinical reference for the prevention and treatment of infant bronchiolitis in northern China. Methods Based on the electronic medical record system, the clinical data of 132 children hospitalized with bronchiolitis at Hebei Children's Hospital from September 2022 to February 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Sputum or nasopharyngeal secretion specimens were collected within 24 h of admission, and multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was performed to detect common respiratory pathogens. Patients were divided into a pathogen-tested group (112 cases) and a pathogen-untested group (20 cases). The tested group comprised a positive subgroup of 99 cases (77 single infections and 22 mixed infections) and a negative subgroup of 13 cases. Clinical recovery evaluation: clinical recovery speed was evaluated using the hospital length of stay (LOS); patients were categorized into a rapid-recovery group (LOS ≤ 5 days) and a delayed-recovery group (LOS > 5 days). To avoid selection bias arising from missing pathogen data, all analyses examining the association between pathogen profile and LOS were restricted to the 112 pathogen-tested patients; descriptive demographic characteristics (Section 3.1 ) were based on the full cohort of 132 patients. A subsequent sensitivity analysis (Section 3.1.1 ) found no statistically significant differences between the 20 untested and 112 tested patients in sex, age, LOS, or rapid-/delayed-recovery group composition, suggesting a limited risk of residual selection bias from this approach. Results Among the 132 children with bronchiolitis, the median age was 6.6 months and the median LOS was 6.0 days. In the tested group (112 cases), the overall positive rate was 88.4% (99/112), with single infection accounting for 68.8% (77/112), mixed infection accounting for 19.6% (22/112), and negative results accounting for 11.6% (13/112). The top three detected pathogens were respiratory syncytial virus (RSV, 54.5%), human rhinovirus (HRV, 31.3%), and parainfluenza virus (PIV, 6.3%), with RSV/HRV (11 cases) being the most common mixed infection. RSV and mixed infections exhibited a bimodal epidemic feature during the study period: in addition to the traditional winter-spring heating season (November to March of the following year), an atypical off-season epidemic peak emerged in May, with a single-month RSV detection rate of 82.1% (23/28). In contrast, hospitalized cases were relatively sparse in other months of the summer-autumn season (June to October). Because case ascertainment was not a complete census in every year and sample sizes were limited, the year-to-year stability of this off-season peak was not confirmed; see Section 2.4 and the Discussion. Within the 112 pathogen-tested patients (rapid-recovery group, n = 52; delayed-recovery group, n = 60), infants < 6 months accounted for 55.8% (29/52) of the rapid-recovery group versus 41.7% (25/60) of the delayed-recovery group ( P = 0.1363); RSV positivity was 50.0% (26/52) vs. 58.3% (35/60) ( P = 0.3771), HRV positivity was 30.8% (16/52) vs. 31.7% (19/60) ( P = 0.9186), and mixed-infection rate was 13.5% (7/52) vs. 25.0% (15/60) ( P = 0.1253); none of these differences reached statistical significance. Conclusion RSV and HRV are the core dominant pathogens of hospitalized bronchiolitis in this region. In addition to the traditional winter-spring heating-season peak, an atypical off-season epidemic peak occurred in May, although its year-to-year stability requires further confirmation.

title: Improving respiratory virus forecasts by capturing the effects of school holidays, public holidays and seasonal changes in transmission
abstract: Respiratory viruses impose a substantial burden of morbidity and mortality globally, and models that forecast this burden are widely used to support public health decision-making. However, the public health utility of these forecasts can be limited by poor predictive accuracy. In this work, we show how capturing the effects of school holidays, public holidays and seasonal changes in transmission can improve respiratory virus forecasting performance. We construct a Bayesian renewal model where the effective reproduction number R(t) is composed of log-additive components including school and public holiday effects and an annually-periodic Gaussian process. The model also allows for the relative rate of reporting to vary with school and public holidays. We use this model to forecast respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza and SARS-CoV-2 case incidence across a 28-day horizon over five jurisdictions in Australia. Applied to the 2025 winter season, our forecasts outperform a random-walk baseline forecast across all settings. We find that the inclusion of holiday and seasonal transmission effects improved forecasting performance across the three pathogens. We show that the school holidays are associated with population-wide reductions in R(t) on the order of 5-15% but are generally not associated with changes in reporting. Collectively, our results provide support for the inclusion of holiday and seasonal effects in future respiratory virus forecasting models.

title: A New Homogeneous Surrogate Virus Neutralization Test Format Based on Liposomes and the Complement System
abstract: Abstract Neutralizing antibodies are key mediators of protection against common viral infections such as SARS-CoV-2, influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), making them an important target for diagnostic assays assessing immune status and vaccine efficacy. Here we present a novel platform technology that specifically detects SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibodies in a simple homogeneous no-wash format as a surrogate virus neutralization test (sVNT). Liposomes loaded with a quenched fluorophore were modified with the angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) receptor, the main receptor for SARS-CoV-2 entry. Virus surrogates based on the receptor binding domain (RBD) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein were developed that bind to ACE2-liposomes and contain a trigger moiety, which activates the complement system leading to liposome lysis. Neutralizing antibodies inhibit this binding event and thus prevent the generation of a fluorescent signal. The proof-of-principle was demonstrated using SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibodies and pooled human serum, generating IC50 values that can be compared to other assay formats. Testing of 20 SARS-CoV-2 antibody negative sera and 24 sera from individuals with SARS-CoV-2 infection and/or vaccination history, resulted in a specificity of 95%, sensitivity of 96% and a strong correlation (Spearman r = 0.78, Pearson r = 0.77) with antibody titers determined in a pseudovirus neutralization test. The assay platform can be readily adapted to other targets, offering a rapid and straightforward approach to serological immunodiagnostics and in general other competitive assay formats. The simplicity of the assay, the avoidance of washing and immobilization steps renders this format ideally suited for high-throughput screening and point-of-care settings.

title: RSM01, an extended half-life RSV monoclonal antibody with a high barrier to in vitro resistance
abstract: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes substantial infant morbidity and mortality, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). RSM01 is a long-acting RSV monoclonal antibody (mAb) in development for LMICs. In vitro generation of RSM01 resistant mutants has previously been unsuccessful. We systematically assessed the in vitro resistance barrier of RSM01 and the susceptibility of a panel of global contemporary strains to RSM01. Monoclonal antibody resistant mutants (MARMs) were generated by serially passaging triple plaque-purified RSV-A2 and RSV-B1 using HEp-2 cells under pressure from RSM01, nirsevimab, or palivizumab, followed by phenotypic and genotypic characterisation. Moderate resistance was defined as > 3-fold and high resistance as > 30-fold increase in IC 50 compared with parental virus. The susceptibility of contemporary global clinical strains to RSM01 was tested in a neutralisation assay. RSV-A and B strains developed high resistance to palivizumab and nirsevimab, while RSM01 pressure induced moderate resistance. No MARMs demonstrated a fitness advantage. RSM01 neutralised global contemporary strains. In conclusion, in vitro RSM01 resistance was infrequent and moderate and RSM01 had broad activity against circulating strains. The confirmation of the high barrier to resistance of RSM01 is encouraging and provides an alternative should resistance emerge with widespread use of current licensed anti-RSV mAbs.

title_zh: RSM01,一种半衰期延长的 RSV 单克隆抗体,具有高体外耐药屏障
source_body_en: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes substantial infant morbidity and mortality, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). RSM01 is a long-acting RSV monoclonal antibody (mAb) in development for LMICs. In vitro generation of RSM01 resistant mutants has previously been unsuccessful. We systematically assessed the in vitro resistance barrier of RSM01 and the susceptibility of a panel of global contemporary strains to RSM01. Monoclonal antibody resistant mutants (MARMs) were generated by serially passaging triple plaque-purified RSV-A2 and RSV-B1 using HEp-2 cells under pressure from RSM01, nirsevimab, or palivizumab, followed by phenotypic and genotypic characterisation. Moderate resistance was defined as > 3-fold and high resistance as > 30-fold increase in IC 50 compared with parental virus. The susceptibility of contemporary global clinical strains to RSM01 was tested in a neutralisation assay. RSV-A and B strains developed high resistance to palivizumab and nirsevimab, while RSM01 pressure induced moderate resistance. No MARMs demonstrated a fitness advantage. RSM01 neutralised global contemporary strains. In conclusion, in vitro RSM01 resistance was infrequent and moderate and RSM01 had broad activity against circulating strains. The confirmation of the high barrier to resistance of RSM01 is encouraging and provides an alternative should resistance emerge with widespread use of current licensed anti-RSV mAbs.

title: Respiratory viruses detected by real-time PCR at King Abdulaziz University Hospital, Jeddah, 2021 to 2023: a retrospective study of virological, age-related, and clinical characteristics
abstract: Abstract Background Data on respiratory viruses in western Saudi Arabia after the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) mitigation period are limited. We described the viruses detected, their distribution over time and by age, clinical features, pre-existing conditions, and outcomes in a hospital-based series of polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-positive episodes at King Abdulaziz University Hospital (KAUH), Jeddah. Methods We retrospectively reviewed episodes in which at least one respiratory virus was detected by real-time PCR, primarily with a multiplex panel, in nasopharyngeal specimens tested clinically between January 2021 and December 2023; testing denominators were not available. Analyses used exact tests, odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI), Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and Firth logistic regression. Results We analyzed 149 PCR-positive episodes in 143 patients; no records were available for December 2021, January to September 2022, or January 2023. Median age was 9.0 months (interquartile range 3.0 to 29.0; unknown for 32 episodes). Human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) was detected in 40.9% and human rhinovirus/enterovirus (hRV/hEV) in 34.2% of episodes; 16.8% had co-detections. Among episodes with known age, 70.2% of those in infants younger than 6 months were hRSV-positive (q = 0.005); at least 33 of all 61 hRSV episodes occurred in this age group. hRSV and hRV/hEV proportions differed between years, including within October and November, while testing sites also changed. No association between documented symptoms and virus detection remained significant after correction. Pre-existing conditions were documented in 46.3% of episodes and were nominally less frequent with hRSV (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.14 to 0.64), but not after correction (q = 0.057). Specimens were collected in an intensive care unit in 22.4% of episodes; 9 of 143 patients (6.3%) had a recorded death at data extraction. Conclusions In this single-center series of PCR-positive episodes, hRSV and hRV/hEV were the most frequently detected viruses, and, among episodes with known age, hRSV was concentrated in young infants, most without documented pre-existing conditions. Without testing denominators, these data describe the composition of positive detections, not incidence or seasonality; they provide local hospital reference data from before infant hRSV immunization, whose impact will require denominator-based surveillance. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study aimed to analyze respiratory viruses detected by real-time PCR at King Abdulaziz University Hospital, Jeddah, from 2021 to 2023, with a focus on human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human rhinovirus/enterovirus (hRV/hEV). The central question was to determine the virological, age-related, and clinical characteristics of these detections.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study was a retrospective analysis of PCR-positive episodes at KAUH, using real-time PCR with a multiplex panel on nasopharyngeal specimens. The analyses included exact tests, odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI), Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and Firth logistic regression. Testing denominators were not available, and the study included 149 PCR-positive episodes in 143 patients, though no records were available for certain periods.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human rhinovirus/enterovirus (hRV/hEV) were the most frequently detected viruses, with hRSV accounting for 40.9% and hRV/hEV for 34.2% of episodes. Co-detections were observed in 16.8% of cases. Among episodes with known age, hRSV was predominantly found in infants younger than 6 months, with 70.2% of these cases being hRSV-positive. However, no significant association was found between documented symptoms and virus detection after correction for multiple testing.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study notes that without testing denominators, the data describe the composition of positive detections rather than incidence or seasonality. Additionally, the analysis of pre-existing conditions showed a nominal association with hRSV, but this was not significant after correction. The study also highlights that testing sites changed over time, which may affect the interpretation of viral distribution patterns.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest the need for denominator-based surveillance to better understand the incidence and seasonality of hRSV and hRV/hEV. They also provide local hospital reference data from before the introduction of infant hRSV immunization, which could inform future public health strategies and vaccine implementation.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study analyzed respiratory viruses detected by real-time PCR at King Abdulaziz University Hospital in Jeddah from 2021 to 2023. The primary focus was on human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human rhinovirus/enterovirus (hRV/hEV). The study found that hRSV and hRV/hEV were the most frequently detected viruses, with hRSV predominantly affecting infants under six months. However, no significant association was found between symptoms and virus detection after correction. The data, while descriptive, highlight the need for denominator-based surveillance to assess true incidence and seasonality, especially in the context of upcoming hRSV immunization programs.

elements_en.scope_and_question: The study aimed to analyze respiratory viruses detected by real-time PCR at King Abdulaziz University Hospital, Jeddah, from 2021 to 2023, with a focus on human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human rhinovirus/enterovirus (hRV/hEV). The central question was to determine the virological, age-related, and clinical characteristics of these detections.
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study was a retrospective analysis of PCR-positive episodes at KAUH, using real-time PCR with a multiplex panel on nasopharyngeal specimens. The analyses included exact tests, odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI), Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and Firth logistic regression. Testing denominators were not available, and the study included 149 PCR-positive episodes in 143 patients, though no records were available for certain periods.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human rhinovirus/enterovirus (hRV/hEV) were the most frequently detected viruses, with hRSV accounting for 40.9% and hRV/hEV for 34.2% of episodes. Co-detections were observed in 16.8% of cases. Among episodes with known age, hRSV was predominantly found in infants younger than 6 months, with 70.2% of these cases being hRSV-positive. However, no significant association was found between documented symptoms and virus detection after correction for multiple testing.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study notes that without testing denominators, the data describe the composition of positive detections rather than incidence or seasonality. Additionally, the analysis of pre-existing conditions showed a nominal association with hRSV, but this was not significant after correction. The study also highlights that testing sites changed over time, which may affect the interpretation of viral distribution patterns.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest the need for denominator-based surveillance to better understand the incidence and seasonality of hRSV and hRV/hEV. They also provide local hospital reference data from before the introduction of infant hRSV immunization, which could inform future public health strategies and vaccine implementation.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究旨在分析 2021 年至 2023 年吉达阿卜杜勒阿齐兹国王大学医院实时 PCR 检测到的呼吸道病毒,重点是人类 呼吸道合胞病毒 (hRSV) 和人类鼻病毒/肠道病毒 (hRV/hEV)。核心问题是确定这些检测的病毒学、年龄相关和临床特征。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该研究是对 KAUH 的 PCR 阳性事件进行回顾性分析,使用实时 PCR 和多重面板对鼻咽标本进行分析。分析包括精确检验、95% 置信区间 (CI) 的比值比 (OR)、Benjamini-Hochberg 校正和 Firth 逻辑回归。测试分母不可用,该研究包括 143 名患者的 149 次 PCR 阳性事件,但没有特定时期的记录。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 人类 呼吸道合胞病毒 (hRSV) 和人类鼻病毒/肠道病毒 (hRV/hEV) 是最常检测到的病毒,其中 hRSV 占 40.9%,hRV/hEV 占 34.2%。16.8% 的病例中观察到了共同检测。在已知年龄的病例中,hRSV 主要见于 6 个月以下的婴儿,其中 70.2% 的病例为 hRSV 阳性。然而,经过多次检测校正后,没有发现记录的症状和病毒检测之间存在显着关联。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该研究指出,在不测试分母的情况下,数据描述的是阳性检测的组成,而不是 发病率 或季节性。此外,对已有病症的分析显示与 hRSV 存在名义上的关联,但在校正后并不显着。该研究还强调,检测地点随着时间的推移而变化,这可能会影响对病毒分布模式的解释。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果表明,需要基于分母的 发病率 来更好地理解 发病率 以及 hRSV 和 hRV/hEV 的季节性。他们还提供了引入婴儿 hRSV 免疫之前当地医院的参考数据,这可以为未来的公共卫生策略和 疫苗 的实施提供信息。

title_zh: 2021 年至 2023 年吉达阿卜杜勒阿齐兹国王大学医院实时 PCR 检测到的呼吸道病毒:病毒学、年龄相关和临床特征的回顾性研究
source_body_en: Abstract Background Data on respiratory viruses in western Saudi Arabia after the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) mitigation period are limited. We described the viruses detected, their distribution over time and by age, clinical features, pre-existing conditions, and outcomes in a hospital-based series of polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-positive episodes at King Abdulaziz University Hospital (KAUH), Jeddah. Methods We retrospectively reviewed episodes in which at least one respiratory virus was detected by real-time PCR, primarily with a multiplex panel, in nasopharyngeal specimens tested clinically between January 2021 and December 2023; testing denominators were not available. Analyses used exact tests, odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI), Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and Firth logistic regression. Results We analyzed 149 PCR-positive episodes in 143 patients; no records were available for December 2021, January to September 2022, or January 2023. Median age was 9.0 months (interquartile range 3.0 to 29.0; unknown for 32 episodes). Human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) was detected in 40.9% and human rhinovirus/enterovirus (hRV/hEV) in 34.2% of episodes; 16.8% had co-detections. Among episodes with known age, 70.2% of those in infants younger than 6 months were hRSV-positive (q = 0.005); at least 33 of all 61 hRSV episodes occurred in this age group. hRSV and hRV/hEV proportions differed between years, including within October and November, while testing sites also changed. No association between documented symptoms and virus detection remained significant after correction. Pre-existing conditions were documented in 46.3% of episodes and were nominally less frequent with hRSV (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.14 to 0.64), but not after correction (q = 0.057). Specimens were collected in an intensive care unit in 22.4% of episodes; 9 of 143 patients (6.3%) had a recorded death at data extraction. Conclusions In this single-center series of PCR-positive episodes, hRSV and hRV/hEV were the most frequently detected viruses, and, among episodes with known age, hRSV was concentrated in young infants, most without documented pre-existing conditions. Without testing denominators, these data describe the composition of positive detections, not incidence or seasonality; they provide local hospital reference data from before infant hRSV immunization, whose impact will require denominator-based surveillance. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

The target entities are human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), RSV-A, RSV-B, and related subtypes. The review is in the planning stage and does not yet report findings, controversies, or implications. The methodology includes a retrospective registration and focuses on comparative effectiveness and safety of interventions.

title: Post-marketing safety signals of the ROCK2 inhibitor Belumosudil for chronic graft-versus-host disease: a real-world disproportionality analysis based on the FAERS database
abstract: Objective To characterize the real-world post-marketing safety profile, evidence hierarchy, and demographic vulnerabilities of the selective ROCK2 inhibitor Belumosudil in chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) using FAERS. Methods Adverse event reports (Q3 2021–Q4 2025) were extracted from FAERS. To control indication confounding, primary disproportionality analysis was anchored to a disease-restricted cGVHD and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation background ( n = 921 , 529 ) using four consensus algorithms (ROR, PRR, BCPNN, MGPS) with False Discovery Rate (FDR) validation. Signals were filtered via a prespecified clinical protocol and stratified into a three-tier evidence framework. Subgroup vulnerabilities (prognostic mortality, age, sex) were evaluated using Fisher’s exact tests. Dual sensitivity analyses evaluated polypharmacy (monotherapy cohort with standardized mean difference [SMD] balance) and denominator stability (whole-database comparator). Results Among 1,797 primary suspect Belumosudil reports (6,056 adverse events), initial screening identified 61 consensus-positive Preferred Terms (PTs); 60 maintained FDR significance ( q < 0.05 ). After systematically excluding 16 confounded administrative and indication-synonymous terms, 45 core PTs were retained across three tiers (Tier 1 trial verification, n = 6 ; Tier 2 novel mechanistic signals, n = 6 ; Tier 3 clinical confounders, n = 33 ). Pharmacological toxicities clustered into three dimensions: musculoskeletal symptoms (muscle tightness, ROR = 10.25; skin swelling, ROR = 19.32), mucosal/viral infections (respiratory syncytial virus, ROR = 4.02; viral gastroenteritis, ROR = 4.81), and laboratory abnormalities (hepatic enzyme increased, ROR = 5.64; blood immunoglobulin G decreased, ROR = 5.75). Subgroup stratification identified distinct clinical vulnerabilities: fatal cases were enriched for obliterative bronchiolitis and muscle atrophy; elderly patients ( ≥ 65 years) exhibited predilection for joint stiffness and lip pain ( P < 0.05 ); and females displayed heightened susceptibility to transaminase elevation, skin atrophy, and oral mucosal blistering ( P < 0.05 ). Monotherapy sensitivity analysis ( N = 1 , 255 ; almost all baseline SMDs < 0.10 ) and whole-database comparison confirmed signal robustness. Conclusion Belumosudil’s real-world safety landscape is dominated by musculoskeletal tightness and edema, mucosal and viral infections, and transaminase/immunoglobulin fluctuations, without novel systemic organ toxicities. Findings underscore the necessity of tailored clinical surveillance: monitoring pulmonary decline in severe disease, joint stiffness in elderly recipients, and hepatic transaminases in females.

The research aimed to identify safety signals, demographic vulnerabilities, and adverse event patterns. Adverse event reports from Q3 2021 to Q4 2025 were extracted and filtered using four consensus algorithms with FDR validation. The main results showed 61 consensus-positive Preferred Terms (PTs), with 60 maintaining FDR significance. After excluding confounded terms, 45 core PTs were retained, categorized into three tiers. The evidence was robust due to sensitivity analyses, but the study is limited to post-marketing safety signals without direct clinical outcomes.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在利用 FAERS 数据库描述选择性 ROCK2 抑制剂 Belumosudil 在慢性移植物抗 宿主 疾病 (cGVHD) 中的真实上市后安全性特征,满足了解其在临床实践中安全性的需要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用 FAERS 数据库中 2021 年第三季度至 2025 年第四季度的不良事件报告进行了现实世界的不成比例分析,重点关注疾病限制性 cGVHD 和造血干细胞移植背景,有 921,529 条记录。
elements_zh.methods: 不良事件报告从 FAERS 中提取,并通过预先指定的临床方案进行过滤。使用具有错误发现率 (FDR) 验证的四种共识算法(ROR、PRR、BCPNN、MGPS)来识别信号,并使用 Fisher 精确检验评估子组漏洞。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 1,797 份主要可疑贝鲁莫舒地尔报告(6,056 起不良事件)中,初步筛选确定了 61 项共识积极的首选术语 (PT);60 保持 FDR 显着性 (q < 0.05)。经过系统排除后,三层中保留了 45 个核心 PT。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,贝鲁莫舒地尔的安全性主要表现为肌肉骨骼紧张和水肿、粘膜和病毒感染以及转氨酶/免疫球蛋白波动,没有新的全身器官毒性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调了定制临床 监测 的必要性,特别是监测严重疾病中的肺功能衰退、老年接受者的关节僵硬以及女性的肝转氨酶。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 双重敏感性分析证实了信号的稳健性,但该研究仅限于上市后安全信号,不包括直接的临床结果或因果机制。

title: Epidemiological characteristics of 11 respiratory pathogens among 19,382 hospitalized children in Putian city
abstract: Objective To analyze the epidemiological characteristics of common respiratory pathogens among children hospitalized with acute respiratory tract infections (ARTIs) in Putian city with the aim of providing a scientific basis for regional pediatric respiratory infection prevention. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on clinical data from 19,382 children hospitalized at the Affiliated Hospital of Putian University between January 1, 2023, and December 30, 2025. Multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) combined with capillary electrophoresis fragment analysis was employed to detect 11 common respiratory pathogens. Results A total of 19,382 hospitalized children were enrolled, with an overall respiratory pathogen positivity rate of 69.40%. The positivity rate was highest among preschool-aged children and lowest among adolescents. Mycoplasma pneumoniae (Mp) exhibited the highest detection rate in school-aged children (38.57%), while human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) demonstrated the highest detection rate in infants and toddlers (19.53%). The pathogen positivity rate was 70.24% in males and 68.20% in females, with a statistically significant difference between sexes. Among the 19,382 children with ARTIs, single-pathogen detection predominated, accounting for 58.89%; dual-pathogen detection accounted for 9.93%, and multiple-pathogen detection accounted for 0.57%. Respiratory pathogen positivity rates showed seasonal fluctuations, peaking in winter 2023 (73.98%), spring 2024 (77.85%), and autumn 2025 (74.17%). In addition, the positivity rates of influenza A virus (InfA), influenza B virus (InfB) decreased with increasing temperature, whereas those of HRSV, human coronavirus (HCOV) increased with increasing temperature. A total of 15,601 pathogen detection events were recorded; the three most frequently detected pathogens were human rhinovirus (HRV; 24.66%), Mp (23.68%), and HRSV (14.52%). Conclusion The overall positivity rate of respiratory pathogens among children hospitalized with ARTIs in Putian was high (69.40%), with distinct age-related and seasonal characteristics. Mp predominated in school-aged children, whereas HRSV predominated in infants and toddlers. Pathogen detection peaked in autumn–winter 2023, spring 2024, and autumn 2025. HRV, Mp, and HRSV were the three dominant pathogens. The dual- and multiple-detection groups had median hospital stays of 6 days, compared with 5 days in the pathogen-negative and single-detection groups. These findings provide a scientific basis for optimizing clinical diagnosis and treatment of pediatric respiratory infections in this region.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the epidemiological characteristics of 11 respiratory pathogens among 19,382 hospitalized children in Putian city with acute respiratory tract infections (ARTIs) between 2023 and 2025. Human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) had the highest detection rate in infants and toddlers (19.53%), while Mycoplasma pneumoniae (Mp) was most prevalent in school-aged children (38.57%). The positivity rates showed seasonal fluctuations, peaking in winter 2023, spring 2024, and autumn 2025. The study provides insights into the age-related and seasonal patterns of respiratory pathogens, which could inform regional strategies for the prevention and management of pediatric respiratory infections. However, the findings are based on retrospective data, which may limit their generalizability and confidence.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对2023年1月1日至2025年12月30日莆田学院附属医院住院的19382名儿童的临床资料进行回顾性分析。

abstract_zh: 目的分析莆田市急性呼吸道感染(ARTI)住院儿童常见呼吸道病原体的流行病学特征,为区域小儿呼吸道感染的预防提供科学依据。方法 回顾性分析2023年1月1日至2025年12月30日莆田学院附属医院住院的19 382例儿童的临床资料,采用多重聚合酶链式反应(PCR)结合毛细管电泳片段分析法检测11种常见呼吸道病原菌。结果共纳入住院儿童19382例,呼吸道病原总体阳性率为69.40%。学龄前儿童的阳性率最高,青少年最低。肺炎支原体(Mp)在学龄儿童中检出率最高(38.57%),而人呼吸道合胞病毒(HRSV)在婴幼儿中检出率最高(19.53%)。男性病原体阳性率为70.24%,女性病原体阳性率为68.20%,性别间差异有统计学意义。19382例ARTI儿童中,单一病原检测为主,占58.89%;双病原检测占9.93%,多病原检测占0.57%。呼吸道病原体阳性率呈现季节性波动,峰值出现在2023年冬季(73.98%)、2024年春季(77.85%)和2025年秋季(74.17%)。此外,甲型流感病毒(InfA)、乙型流感病毒(InfB)的阳性率随温度升高而降低,而HRSV、人类冠状病毒(HCOV)的阳性率随温度升高而升高。共记录病原体检测事件15601起;三种最常见的病原体是人鼻病毒(HRV;24.66%)、Mp(23.68%)和HRSV(14.52%)。结论 莆田市ARTIs住院儿童呼吸道病原体总体阳性率较高(69.40%),且具有明显的年龄和季节特征。Mp 在学龄儿童中占主导地位,而 HRSV 在婴儿和幼儿中占主导地位。病原体检测高峰期为2023年秋冬、2024年春季和2025年秋季。HRV、Mp和HRSV是三大主要病原体。双重和多重检测组的中位住院时间为 6 天,而病原体阴性和单一检测组的中位住院时间为 5 天。这些研究结果为优化该地区小儿呼吸道感染临床诊断和治疗提供了科学依据。

title: KẾT QUẢ ĐIỀU TRỊ VIÊM PHỔI SƠ SINH NHIỄM VIRUS HỢP BÀO HÔ HẤP VÀ MỘT SỐ YẾU TỐ LIÊN QUAN TẠI BỆNH VIỆN NHI TRUNG ƯƠNG
abstract: Mục tiêu: Nhận xét kết quả điều trị và một số yếu tố liên quan đến viêm phổi sơ sinh nhiễm virus hợp bào hô hấp (Respiratory Syncytial Virus - RSV) tại Bệnh viện Nhi Trung ương năm 2025-2026. Đối tượng và phương pháp: Nghiên cứu mô tả tiến cứu 202 trẻ sơ sinh viêm phổi RSV dương tính, điều trị nội trú tại Trung tâm Sơ sinh, Bệnh viện Nhi Trung ương từ 10/2025-7/2026. Kết quả: 98,0% đỡ, giảm/khỏi; 2,0% đỡ chuyển tuyến; 0% tử vong, 53,5% cần hỗ trợ hô hấp. Thời gian nằm viện trung vị 7,0 ngày. Thời gian hỗ trợ hô hấp tăng dần theo phương thức hỗ trợ hô hấp cao nhất được dùng. Yếu tố độc lập liên quan hỗ trợ hô hấp: SpO2 thấp, độ tuổi, thời gian diễn biến bệnh trước nhập viện dài. Yếu tố độc lập liên quan thời gian nằm viện: bệnh kèm theo (tim bẩm sinh), CRP >= 10mg/L, độ tuổi (p < 0,05). Kết luận: Kết quả điều trị khả quan. SpO2 thấp, tuổi nhỏ, tim bẩm sinh và CRP tăng là yếu tố quan trọng trong tiên lượng.

analysis.study_design_and_population: Đây là một nghiên cứu mô tả tiến cứu được thực hiện trên 202 trẻ sơ sinh mắc viêm phổi RSV dương tính, được điều trị nội trú tại Trung tâm Sơ sinh, Bệnh viện Nhi Trung ương từ tháng 10 năm 2025 đến tháng 7 năm 2026.
analysis.methods: Nghiên cứu sử dụng dữ liệu từ các trẻ sơ sinh được chẩn đoán viêm phổi RSV và điều trị tại bệnh viện, bao gồm theo dõi thời gian nằm viện, mức độ hỗ trợ hô hấp và các yếu tố liên quan như SpO2, độ tuổi và CRP.
analysis.main_results: 98,0% trẻ sơ sinh có triệu chứng giảm/khỏi, 2,0% đỡ chuyển tuyến, 0% tử vong và 53,5% cần hỗ trợ hô hấp. Thời gian nằm viện trung vị là 7,0 ngày. Thời gian hỗ trợ hô hấp tăng dần theo phương thức hỗ trợ hô hấp cao nhất được dùng.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Kết quả cho thấy tỷ lệ điều trị thành công cao, nhưng thời gian hỗ trợ hô hấp và thời gian nằm viện phụ thuộc vào mức độ nghiêm trọng của bệnh và các yếu tố như SpO2, độ tuổi và tình trạng bệnh kèm theo.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Kết quả cung cấp thông tin quan trọng về tiên lượng và các yếu tố nguy cơ trong điều trị viêm phổi sơ sinh do RSV, hỗ trợ trong việc lập kế hoạch chăm sóc và theo dõi bệnh nhân.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Nghiên cứu mang tính mô tả, không có dữ liệu thống kê sâu hơn hoặc phân tích nguyên nhân cụ thể, do đó mức độ tin cậy được đánh giá là trung bình.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to evaluate treatment outcomes and related factors in neonatal pneumonia cases caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) at the National Children's Hospital from October 2025 to July 2026. A descriptive prospective study was conducted on 202 neonates with RSV-positive pneumonia admitted for inpatient treatment. The results showed that 98.0% of cases improved, 2.0% were transferred to another ward, and 0% resulted in mortality. Approximately 53.5% of patients required respiratory support, with a median hospitalization duration of 7.0 days. The time of respiratory support increased with the highest mode of support used. Independent factors associated with respiratory support included low SpO2, age, and prolonged disease duration before admission. Independent factors linked to hospitalization duration were congenital heart disease, CRP ≥ 10mg/L, and age (p < 0.05). The authors concluded that treatment outcomes were favorable, but low SpO2, young age, congenital heart disease, and elevated CRP were important predictors of prognosis. The study's descriptive nature and lack of detailed statistical analysis limit the confidence in its findings, resulting in a moderate evidence strength assessment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 病毒感染者hợp bào hô hấp (RSV) gây ra tại Bệnh viện Nhi Trung ương trong giai đoạn 2025-2026。

elements_zh.methods: Nghiên cứu sử dụng dữ liệu từ các trẻ sơ sinh được chẩn đoán viêm phổi RSV và điều trị tại bệnh viện,bao我建议您使用 SpO2、CRP 和 CRP。

title_zh: 2025-2026年呼吸道合胞病毒毛细支气管炎新生儿肺炎治疗结果及相关因素分析
source_body_en: Mục tiêu: Nhận xét kết quả điều trị và một số yếu tố liên quan đến viêm phổi sơ sinh nhiễm virus hợp bào hô hấp (Respiratory Syncytial Virus - RSV) tại Bệnh viện Nhi Trung ương năm 2025-2026. Đối tượng và phương pháp: Nghiên cứu mô tả tiến cứu 202 trẻ sơ sinh viêm phổi RSV dương tính, điều trị nội trú tại Trung tâm Sơ sinh, Bệnh viện Nhi Trung ương từ 10/2025-7/2026. Kết quả: 98,0% đỡ, giảm/khỏi; 2,0% đỡ chuyển tuyến; 0% tử vong, 53,5% cần hỗ trợ hô hấp. Thời gian nằm viện trung vị 7,0 ngày. Thời gian hỗ trợ hô hấp tăng dần theo phương thức hỗ trợ hô hấp cao nhất được dùng. Yếu tố độc lập liên quan hỗ trợ hô hấp: SpO2 thấp, độ tuổi, thời gian diễn biến bệnh trước nhập viện dài. Yếu tố độc lập liên quan thời gian nằm viện: bệnh kèm theo (tim bẩm sinh), CRP >= 10mg/L, độ tuổi (p < 0,05). Kết luận: Kết quả điều trị khả quan. SpO2 thấp, tuổi nhỏ, tim bẩm sinh và CRP tăng là yếu tố quan trọng trong tiên lượng.

title: Diversification without convergence: national childhood respiratory pathogen spectra diverge as they diversify, 1990-2023
abstract: Background National childhood respiratory pathogen spectra are diversifying nearly everywhere - within-country diversity rose in 203 of 204 countries between 1990 and 2023 - yet whether countries are diversifying toward a common spectrum or along divergent paths is unknown. We quantified between-country compositional distance of national pathogen spectra over the same period. Methods We built national pathogen share vectors from Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 lower respiratory infection etiologic attributions (26 pathogens, 204 countries, ages 0-19 years) at five timepoints spanning 1990-2023. Between-country distance was measured as all pairwise Jensen-Shannon divergences (JSD; primary) and Bray-Curtis dissimilarities, with Baselga and Jaccard decompositions; robustness was assessed across metrics, pathogen panels, low-count thresholds and a balanced panel of 107 countries. Results Mean pairwise JSD rose from 0.0084 in 1990 to 0.0283 in 2023 (+238%; trend p = 0.030), peaking in 2021 (+283%) with a partial 2023 pullback. Bray-Curtis dissimilarity rose +120% and the balanced panel +423%. Divergence was entirely balanced variation (share reallocation), with spectrum richness rising from 18.5 to 21.1 of 26 pathogens. Dispersion rose fastest for influenza (coefficient of variation 0.03 to 0.55) and respiratory syncytial virus (0.08 to 0.48). Within-region distance rose in every computable GBD super-region (five of seven): divergence occurs within regions, not between blocs. A country-level bootstrap confirmed the increase (+238%, 95% CI +165 to +331), and segmented trend analysis found no supported breakpoint, with divergence proceeding steadily at +4.1% per year (95% CI 2.0-6.3) rather than in stages. Conclusions National spectra are re-sorting along country-specific axes as vaccine-preventable dominance recedes at different speeds. Diversification is universal, but convergence is absent: the transition at the etiologic-spectrum level is asynchronous and path-dependent, with implications for empirical treatment policy and pathogen surveillance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether national childhood respiratory pathogen spectra are diversifying toward a common spectrum or along divergent paths, as within-country diversity has risen in 203 of 204 countries between 1990 and 2023.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed national pathogen spectra across 204 countries and five timepoints spanning 1990-2023, using data from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 on lower respiratory infection etiologic attributions.
analysis.methods: National pathogen share vectors were constructed from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 data, and between-country compositional distance was measured using Jensen-Shannon divergences and Bray-Curtis dissimilarities, with robustness assessed across multiple metrics and pathogen panels.
analysis.main_results: The mean pairwise Jensen-Shannon divergence increased from 0.0084 in 1990 to 0.0283 in 2023 (+238%; trend p = 0.030), peaking in 2021 (+283%) with a partial 2023 pullback. Spectrum richness rose from 18.5 to 21.1 of 26 pathogens.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that national spectra are re-sorting along country-specific axes, with vaccine-preventable dominance receding at different speeds, indicating an asynchronous and path-dependent transition at the etiologic-spectrum level.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have implications for empirical treatment policy and pathogen surveillance, highlighting the need for tailored approaches to address the divergent diversification of respiratory pathogen spectra across countries.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is based on abstract-only data, and the increase in divergence was confirmed by a country-level bootstrap, with a moderate confidence level due to the lack of detailed statistical procedures and potential biases in the data.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the diversification of national childhood respiratory pathogen spectra from 1990 to 2023, revealing that divergence is occurring along country-specific axes rather than toward a common spectrum. Using data from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023, the researchers measured compositional distance with Jensen-Shannon divergences and Bray-Curtis dissimilarities, finding a significant rise in mean pairwise divergence from 0.0084 in 1990 to 0.0283 in 2023. The results indicate that the diversification is driven by balanced variation in pathogen shares, with spectrum richness increasing from 18.5 to 21.1 of 26 pathogens. The authors suggest that this asynchronous transition has important implications for treatment policy and surveillance. However, the study is based on abstract-only data, and the findings are supported by a country-level bootstrap, which provides moderate confidence. The study highlights the need for tailored approaches to address the divergent patterns of respiratory pathogen spectra across countries.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether national childhood respiratory pathogen spectra are diversifying toward a common spectrum or along divergent paths, as within-country diversity has risen in 203 of 204 countries between 1990 and 2023.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed national pathogen spectra across 204 countries and five timepoints spanning 1990-2023, using data from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 on lower respiratory infection etiologic attributions.
elements_en.methods: National pathogen share vectors were constructed from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 data, and between-country compositional distance was measured using Jensen-Shannon divergences and Bray-Curtis dissimilarities, with robustness assessed across multiple metrics and pathogen panels.
elements_en.main_results: The mean pairwise Jensen-Shannon divergence increased from 0.0084 in 1990 to 0.0283 in 2023 (+238%; trend p = 0.030), peaking in 2021 (+283%) with a partial 2023 pullback. Spectrum richness rose from 18.5 to 21.1 of 26 pathogens.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that national spectra are re-sorting along country-specific axes, with vaccine-preventable dominance receding at different speeds, indicating an asynchronous and path-dependent transition at the etiologic-spectrum level.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have implications for empirical treatment policy and pathogen surveillance, highlighting the need for tailored approaches to address the divergent diversification of respiratory pathogen spectra across countries.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is based on abstract-only data, and the increase in divergence was confirmed by a country-level bootstrap, with a moderate confidence level due to the lack of detailed statistical procedures and potential biases in the data.

title_zh: 多样化但不趋同:国家儿童呼吸道病原体谱随着多样化而出现分歧,1990-2023 年
source_body_en: Background National childhood respiratory pathogen spectra are diversifying nearly everywhere - within-country diversity rose in 203 of 204 countries between 1990 and 2023 - yet whether countries are diversifying toward a common spectrum or along divergent paths is unknown. We quantified between-country compositional distance of national pathogen spectra over the same period. Methods We built national pathogen share vectors from Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 lower respiratory infection etiologic attributions (26 pathogens, 204 countries, ages 0-19 years) at five timepoints spanning 1990-2023. Between-country distance was measured as all pairwise Jensen-Shannon divergences (JSD; primary) and Bray-Curtis dissimilarities, with Baselga and Jaccard decompositions; robustness was assessed across metrics, pathogen panels, low-count thresholds and a balanced panel of 107 countries. Results Mean pairwise JSD rose from 0.0084 in 1990 to 0.0283 in 2023 (+238%; trend p = 0.030), peaking in 2021 (+283%) with a partial 2023 pullback. Bray-Curtis dissimilarity rose +120% and the balanced panel +423%. Divergence was entirely balanced variation (share reallocation), with spectrum richness rising from 18.5 to 21.1 of 26 pathogens. Dispersion rose fastest for influenza (coefficient of variation 0.03 to 0.55) and respiratory syncytial virus (0.08 to 0.48). Within-region distance rose in every computable GBD super-region (five of seven): divergence occurs within regions, not between blocs. A country-level bootstrap confirmed the increase (+238%, 95% CI +165 to +331), and segmented trend analysis found no supported breakpoint, with divergence proceeding steadily at +4.1% per year (95% CI 2.0-6.3) rather than in stages. Conclusions National spectra are re-sorting along country-specific axes as vaccine-preventable dominance recedes at different speeds. Diversification is universal, but convergence is absent: the transition at the etiologic-spectrum level is asynchronous and path-dependent, with implications for empirical treatment policy and pathogen surveillance.
abstract_zh: 背景 几乎所有国家的儿童呼吸道病原体谱系都在多样化——1990 年至 2023 年间,204 个国家中的 203 个国家的国内多样性有所增加——但各国是朝着共同谱系多样化还是沿着不同路径多样化尚不清楚。我们量化了同一时期国家病原体谱的国家间组成距离。方法 我们根据 2023 年全球疾病负担研究下呼吸道感染病因归因(26 个病原体,204 个国家,年龄 0-19 岁)在 1990 年至 2023 年的五个时间点建立了国家病原体份额 媒介。国家间距离通过所有成对的 Jensen-Shannon 散度(JSD;主要)和 Bray-Curtis 差异进行测量,并采用 Baselga 和 Jaccard 分解;稳健性通过指标、病原体小组、低计数阈值和 107 个国家的平衡小组进行了评估。结果 平均成对 JSD 从 1990 年的 0.0084 上升至 2023 年的 0.0283(+238%;趋势 p = 0.030),于 2021 年达到峰值(+283%),并于 2023 年部分回落。Bray-Curtis 差异增加了 +120%,平衡面板增加了 +423%。分歧是完全平衡的变异(份额重新分配),26 种病原体的谱丰富度从 18.5 上升到 21.1。流感(变异系数 0.03 至 0.55)和 呼吸道合胞病毒(变异系数 0.08 至 0.48)的离散度上升最快。每个可计算的 GBD 超级区域(七个中的五个)的区域内距离都增加了:分歧发生在区域内部,而不是集团之间。国家级引导程序证实了这一增长(+238%,95% CI +165 至 +331),分段趋势分析发现没有受支持的断点,分歧以每年 +4.1% 的速度稳定进行(95% CI 2.0-6.3),而不是分阶段进行。结论 随着 疫苗 可预防的主导地位以不同的速度消退,国家频谱正在沿着国家特定轴重新排序。多样化是普遍的,但缺乏趋同性:病因谱水平的转变是异步的和路径依赖的,对经验性的 治疗 政策和病原体 监测 具有影响。

title: Rising Tuberculosis Presentations in Ontario, Canada Are Not Explained by Community SARS-CoV-2 Activity: A Population-Based Time-Series Study
abstract: Background: Tuberculosis (TB) notifications have increased in several high-income countries since 2020. Proposed explanations include pandemic related disruption of treatment for latent tuberculosis, changes in population composition, and immune dysfunction following SARS CoV 2 infection. We assessed whether TB presentations increased during the pandemic era and then tested whether community SARS CoV 2 activity was followed by increased mycobacterial disease. Methods: We conducted a population-based ecological time-series study of first TB- and nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM)-coded hospital, emergency-department and ambulatory clinic presentations in the Greater Toronto/Hamilton Area Plus (GTHA+), Ontario (2024 population approximately 11.2 million), from April 2011 through March 2024. NTM served as a comparator because it shares diagnostic pathways with TB but differs epidemiologically. Negative binomial projection and full-series models estimated pandemic-era changes under three alternative trend assumptions. Distributed lag non linear models estimated cumulative rate ratios for standardized community viral activity over 0 to 12 weeks; sensitivity analyses extended the maximum lag to 26 and 52 weeks. Influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) were prespecified comparators; data for five additional viral exposures were obtained after the primary analysis was completed and analysed as exploratory comparisons. Results: We identified 3,985 first TB-coded and 5,214 first NTM-coded acute-care presentations. Across six models, estimated pandemic-era TB increases ranged from 3% to 22%. No model suggested an increased in NTM. SARS-CoV-2 activity was not positively associated with TB (cumulative rate ratio per 1-SD increase over 0 to 12 weeks 0.909, 95% CI 0.822 to 1.006) or NTM (0.953, 0.868 to 1.047). No positive associations were identified in subgroup analyses or with maximum lags of 26 or 52 weeks. Influenza was not associated with either outcome. RSV was associated with TB and NTM; only the RSV/NTM association met the Bonferroni threshold among the prespecified comparisons, and no exploratory associations met the experiment wide threshold. Conclusions: We identified a modest pandemic era increase in TB-coded acute-care presentations in Ontario, Canada, although its estimated size depended on assumptions about underlying trends. NTM-coded presentations did not increase. Community SARS-CoV-2 activity was not positively associated with subsequent TB or NTM presentations at lags of up to one year and did not provide a temporal explanation for the population-level TB increase. Individual-level effects cannot be excluded.

title_zh: 加拿大安大略省不断上升的结核病报告不能用社区 SARS-CoV-2 活动来解释:一项基于人群的时间序列研究
source_body_en: Background: Tuberculosis (TB) notifications have increased in several high-income countries since 2020. Proposed explanations include pandemic related disruption of treatment for latent tuberculosis, changes in population composition, and immune dysfunction following SARS CoV 2 infection. We assessed whether TB presentations increased during the pandemic era and then tested whether community SARS CoV 2 activity was followed by increased mycobacterial disease. Methods: We conducted a population-based ecological time-series study of first TB- and nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM)-coded hospital, emergency-department and ambulatory clinic presentations in the Greater Toronto/Hamilton Area Plus (GTHA+), Ontario (2024 population approximately 11.2 million), from April 2011 through March 2024. NTM served as a comparator because it shares diagnostic pathways with TB but differs epidemiologically. Negative binomial projection and full-series models estimated pandemic-era changes under three alternative trend assumptions. Distributed lag non linear models estimated cumulative rate ratios for standardized community viral activity over 0 to 12 weeks; sensitivity analyses extended the maximum lag to 26 and 52 weeks. Influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) were prespecified comparators; data for five additional viral exposures were obtained after the primary analysis was completed and analysed as exploratory comparisons. Results: We identified 3,985 first TB-coded and 5,214 first NTM-coded acute-care presentations. Across six models, estimated pandemic-era TB increases ranged from 3% to 22%. No model suggested an increased in NTM. SARS-CoV-2 activity was not positively associated with TB (cumulative rate ratio per 1-SD increase over 0 to 12 weeks 0.909, 95% CI 0.822 to 1.006) or NTM (0.953, 0.868 to 1.047). No positive associations were identified in subgroup analyses or with maximum lags of 26 or 52 weeks. Influenza was not associated with either outcome. RSV was associated with TB and NTM; only the RSV/NTM association met the Bonferroni threshold among the prespecified comparisons, and no exploratory associations met the experiment wide threshold. Conclusions: We identified a modest pandemic era increase in TB-coded acute-care presentations in Ontario, Canada, although its estimated size depended on assumptions about underlying trends. NTM-coded presentations did not increase. Community SARS-CoV-2 activity was not positively associated with subsequent TB or NTM presentations at lags of up to one year and did not provide a temporal explanation for the population-level TB increase. Individual-level effects cannot be excluded.

title: Infant RSV immunity study (IRIS): protocol for a prospective birth cohort in Vancouver, Canada examining how age at respiratory syncytial virus exposure affects how infants respond to the virus immunologically.
abstract: Introduction Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of severe respiratory illness in infants. Age at first infection is strongly associated with disease severity. Infants exposed to RSV at a younger age may not produce an immune response against RSV that is as protective as infection at a later age, and early life infection may influence the risk of recurrent or persistent wheezing, or subsequent asthma. However, how immune development at the time of exposure shapes RSV-specific immunity and long-term respiratory health remains unclear. Methods and analysis The Infant RSV Immunity Study (IRIS) is a prospective birth cohort of 300 healthy infants in British Columbia, Canada, followed to age 3 years. The primary objective is to determine how age at exposure influences RSV-specific immunity and respiratory outcomes. Infants are enrolled in April–June or September–November so that they enter the peak RSV season at either more than 6 months or less than 6 months of age. Symptom-triggered oropharyngeal nasal swabs and post-season RSV serology will identify RSV infections. Birth, pre-season dried blood spot and post-season blood samples will assess RSV-specific antibody, neutralisation, functional antibody and T-cell responses. Clinical outcomes include medically attended respiratory illness, RSV hospitalisation, daily wheezing and inhaler use, and asthma risk at age 3 assessed using the Childhood Asthma Risk Tool. A subgroup of infants will undergo infection-timed blood samples ⁓2 weeks into their first RSV infection. Maternal RSV vaccination and antibody status will be examined as determinants of infant responses. A microbiome upper-airway sample will be collected from the infant at 2 weeks, pre-season and post-season, and around PCR-confirmed RSV infection. In addition, serial stool samples will be collected at 2 weeks, 3, 6, 9 and 12 months of age. Analyses will distinguish developmental, seasonal and infection-associated influences on microbiome and immune development trajectories and test associations with antiviral responses, disease severity and recurrent wheezing post-RSV infection. Infants’ diet will be assessed by serial questionnaires, as another determinant of microbiome development. Ethics and dissemination The study was approved by the University of British Columbia Children’s and Women’s Research Ethics Board (H25-02623). Findings will be disseminated through publications, scientific meetings and participant communication. Trial registration number NCT07653347.

abstract_zh: 简介 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是婴儿严重呼吸道疾病的主要原因。首次感染的年龄与疾病的严重程度密切相关。在较年轻时接触 RSV 的婴儿可能不会产生像晚年感染那样具有保护作用的针对 RSV 的 免疫应答,并且早期感染可能会影响复发性或持续性喘息或随后的哮喘的风险。然而,暴露时的免疫发育如何影响 RSV 特异性免疫和长期呼吸道健康仍不清楚。方法与分析 婴儿 RSV 免疫研究 (IRIS) 是对加拿大不列颠哥伦比亚省 300 名健康婴儿进行的一项预期出生 队列研究,随访至 3 岁。主要目标是确定暴露年龄如何影响 RSV 特异性免疫和呼吸系统结果。婴儿在 4 月至 6 月或 9 月至 11 月入学,以便他们在 6 个月以上或 6 个月以下时进入 RSV 高峰季节。症状触发的口咽鼻拭子和季后 RSV 血清学 将识别 RSV 感染。出生、季前干血斑和季后血液样本将评估 RSV 特异性抗体、中和、功能抗体和 T 细胞反应。临床结果包括呼吸系统疾病的就医、呼吸道合胞病毒住院、每日喘息和吸入器的使用,以及使用儿童哮喘风险工具评估的 3 岁时哮喘风险。一部分婴儿将在首次感染 RSV 后 ⁓2 周接受感染定时血液样本。母体 RSV 疫苗接种 和抗体状态将作为婴儿反应的决定因素进行检查。我们将在婴儿出生后 2 周、赛季前和赛季后以及 PCR 确认的 RSV 感染前后采集微生物组上呼吸道样本。此外,还将在 2 周、3、6、9 和 12 个月大时收集系列粪便样本。分析将区分发育、季节性和感染相关对微生物组和免疫发育轨迹的影响,并测试与 抗病毒药物 反应、疾病严重程度和 RSV 感染后反复喘息的关联。婴儿的饮食将通过系列调查问卷进行评估,作为微生物组发育的另一个决定因素。伦理与传播 该研究得到了不列颠哥伦比亚大学儿童和妇女研究伦理委员会 (H25-02623) 的批准。研究结果将通过出版物、科学会议和参与者交流来传播。试用注册号NCT07653347。

title: A one-step multiplex real-time reverse transcription quantitative PCR assay for rapid and simultaneous detection of human parainfluenza virus, human metapneumovirus, and rhinovirus in patients with acute respiratory tract infection
abstract:
Objective

Clinically, acute respiratory tract infections (ARIs) caused by human parainfluenza virus (PIV), human metapneumovirus (MPV), and human rhinoviruses (HRV) are often indistinguishable due to overlapping symptoms. This study aimed to develop a one-step multiplex real-time RT-qPCR assay for simultaneous, rapid, and accurate detection of PIV (types 1-4), MPV (subgroups A and B), and HRV (species A and B).

Methods

A one-step multiplex real-time RT-qPCR assay was established for simultaneous detection of PIV, MPV, and HRV in clinical specimens. Primers and probes targeted conserved genomic regions, and an internal reference gene (B2M) was included for quality assurance. The limit of detection was determined via serial dilution of standard strains. Assay specificity was verified using 14 non-target pathogens, and repeatability was evaluated across various specimen concentrations. Clinical validation involved comparison with a commercial kit, with sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, agreement rate, and Kappa coefficient calculated for assessment.

Results

A one-step multiplex real-time RT-qPCR assay was successfully developed for the simultaneous detection of PIV, MPV, and HRV. The assay demonstrated a detection limit of 100 copies/mL for all three targets, expressed as the equivalent concentration in the original specimen before nucleic acid extraction; this LOD was determined under multiplex co-amplification conditions, with all three targets present in the same reaction tube at every concentration level. No cross-reactivity was observed against the 14 specified non-target pathogens under the conditions evaluated, and all eight target strains were detected. Repeatability testing showed coefficients of variation (CV) of ≤ 2% for Ct values at low and medium concentrations. At the individual-target level, the sensitivity of the developed assay was 98.82% for HRV, 98.55% for PIV, and 100.0% for MPV, with specificity of 100.0% for all three targets. Pooled (target-level) sensitivity and specificity were 99.06% and 100.0%, respectively, and the overall agreement with the reference method was 99.24% (260/262).

Conclusion

The method provides a technical approach for the simultaneous detection of PIV, MPV, and HRV species A and B. Its clinical utility relative to comprehensive respiratory pathogen panels remains to be established.

full_text: Abstract Background During the 2024/2025 respiratory virus season, Belgium recorded the highest incidence of general practitioner visits for influenza-like illness since the COVID-19 pandemic. The pressure on healthcare systems was driven by epidemics of influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), while SARS-CoV-2 activity remained at low levels. This exceptional situation was observed through conventional surveillance as well as via a novel wastewater-based surveillance program integrating influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 measurements. Methods The innovative program monitors over 4.5 million inhabitants, representing 38% of the Belgian population, on a weekly basis by analysing samples from 30 wastewater treatment plants. The present study aims to validate wastewater data on influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 by comparing it with conventional surveillances. Wastewater-based epidemiological thresholds were computed using a quartile method. Results Throughout the entire season, high levels of correlation were observed between wastewater data and cases confirmed by sentinel laboratories. Wastewater-based thresholds effectively monitored viruses circulation. Conclusions Wastewater-based data was assessed to provide information of added value for monitoring SARS-CoV-2 through wastewater compared to conventional surveillance, offering a large and general population coverage, a short and constant reporting time, and a feature for pandemic preparedness. Several perspectives are proposed in this work to increase the quality of RSV and influenza wastewater monitoring. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to validate wastewater-based surveillance data for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza and SARS-CoV-2 by comparing it with conventional surveillance methods, as Belgium experienced a high incidence of influenza-like illness during the 2024/2025 winter season.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Belgium during the 2024/2025 winter season, involving wastewater samples from 30 treatment plants covering over 4.5 million inhabitants, which represents 38% of the Belgian population.
analysis.methods: Wastewater-based epidemiological thresholds were computed using a quartile method, and the data were compared with conventional surveillance data from sentinel laboratories to validate the effectiveness of the wastewater-based approach.
analysis.main_results: High levels of correlation were observed between wastewater data and cases confirmed by sentinel laboratories throughout the entire season, indicating that wastewater-based thresholds effectively monitored virus circulation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating that wastewater-based data provides added value for monitoring RSV, influenza and SARS-CoV-2, offering large population coverage, short reporting time, and a feature for pandemic preparedness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the implementation of wastewater-based surveillance for RSV, influenza and SARS-CoV-2, enhancing public health preparedness and response to respiratory virus outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on sentinel laboratory data for comparison, and the evidence is moderate as it does not include detailed statistical analyses or long-term validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study validates the use of wastewater-based surveillance for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza, and SARS-CoV-2 in Belgium during the 2024/2025 winter season. The research highlights the effectiveness of wastewater data in monitoring virus circulation, with high correlation observed between wastewater measurements and sentinel laboratory results. The authors emphasize the added value of this approach for public health, offering broad population coverage and rapid reporting. However, the study's evidence is moderate due to its reliance on conventional surveillance data for comparison and the absence of detailed statistical analyses. The findings suggest that wastewater-based surveillance could enhance pandemic preparedness and provide a complementary tool for monitoring respiratory viruses.

analysis_zh.methods: 使用四分位法计算基于废水的流行病学阈值,并将数据与来自哨点实验室的传统 监测 数据进行比较,以验证基于废水的方法的有效性。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在整个季节中,废水数据与哨点实验室确认的病例之间观察到高度相关性,这表明基于废水的阈值可以有效监测病毒传播。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证明基于废水的数据为监测 RSV、流感和 SARS-CoV-2 提供了附加值,提供了大的人口覆盖范围、短的报告时间以及大流行防范的功能。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可为针对 RSV、流感和 SARS-CoV-2 的基于废水的 监测 的实施提供参考,从而加强公共卫生准备和对呼吸道病毒 暴发 的应对。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究由于依赖哨点实验室数据进行比较而受到限制,并且证据有限,因为它不包括详细的统计分析或长期验证。
